text: 祇園精舎の鐘の聲、諸行無常の響あり。娑羅雙樹の花の色、盛者必衰のことわりをあらはす。おごれる人も久しからず、唯春の夜の夢のごとし。たけき者も遂にほろびぬ、偏に風の前の塵に同じ。遠く異朝をとぶらへば、秦の趙高、漢の王莽、梁の周伊、唐の禄山、是等は皆舊主先皇の政にもしたがはず、樂みをきはめ、諫をおもひいれず、天下のみだれむ事をさとらずして、民間の愁る所をしらざりしかば、久からずして亡じし者ども也。近く本朝をうかがふに、承平の將門、天慶の純友、康和の義親、平治の信頼、此等はおごれる心もたけき事も皆とりどりにこそありしかども、まぢかくは六波羅の入道、前太政大臣平朝臣清盛公と申し人のありさま、傳へうけたまはるこそ心も詞も及ばれね。

annotation.translation: The sound of the bells of the Shakyamuni temple resounds with the impermanence of all things. The color of the flowers of the Sal trees reveals the principle that the prosperous must decline. Arrogant people do not last long; they are like dreams on a spring night. The mighty are finally destroyed, exactly like dust before the wind. Looking far back to foreign dynasties, Zhao Gao of Qin, Wang Mang of Han, Zhou Yi of Liang, and An Lushan of Tang—all these did not follow the policies of their former sovereigns and emperors, indulged in pleasure to the limit, disregarded remonstrance, failed to realize that the world would descend into chaos, and were unaware of the people's suffering; thus they perished shortly after. Looking more closely at our own country, Shōhei's Shōmon, Tenkyō's Jun'yū, Kōwa's Yoshichika, and Heiji's Yoritada—all these possessed arrogance and might in their own ways, yet even so, when it comes to the true nature of Rokuhara no Nyūdō, the former Dajō-daijin, Taira no Kiyomori, the records fall short, both in heart and in words.

text: 其先祖を尋ぬれば、桓武天皇第五の皇子、一品式部卿葛原親王九代の後胤讃岐守正盛が孫、刑部卿忠盛朝臣の嫡男なり。彼親王の御子、高親王無官無位にして、うせ給ひぬ。其御子高望の王の時始めて平の姓を給て、上總介になり給しより、忽に王氏を出て人臣につらなる。其子鎭守府將軍義茂後には國香とあらたむ。國香より正盛に至る迄、六代は諸國の受領たりしかども、殿上の仙籍をばいまだゆるされず。

annotation.translation: If one traces their ancestors, they are the great-grandson of Saneaki, the Governor of Sanuki, the eldest son of Tadanori, the Minister of the Department of Punishment, who was the ninth-generation descendant of Prince Kusahara, the fifth son of Emperor Kanmu and the First Rank Minister of the Department of Rites. That Prince's son, Prince Takakura, died without office or rank. At the time of his son Prince Takamochi, the name 'Taira' was first granted to them, and from the time they became the Governor of Kazusa, they suddenly descended from the imperial clan to become subjects. Their son, Yoshimochi, the General of the Headquarters for the Defense of the North, later changed his name to Kunika. From Kunika to Saneaki, six generations served as provincial governors, yet they had not yet been permitted to enter the ranks of the court nobility.

text: しかるを忠盛備前守たりし時、鳥羽院の御願得長壽院を造進して三十三間の御堂をたて、一千一體の御佛をすゑ奉る。供養は天承元年三月十三日なり。勸賞には闕國を給ふべき由仰下されける。境節但馬國のあきたりけるを給にけり。上皇御感のあまりに内の昇殿をゆるさる。忠盛三十六にて始て昇殿す。雲の上人是を嫉み、同き年の十一月廿三日、五節豐明の節會の夜、忠盛を闇討にせむとぞ擬せられける。忠盛是を傳へ聞て、「われ右筆の身にあらず、武勇の家に生れて、今不慮の恥にあはむ事、家の爲、身の爲、こゝろうかるべし。せむずるところ、身を全して君に仕といふ本文あり。」とて、兼て用意をいたす。參内のはじめより大なる鞘卷を用意して束帶のしたにしどけなげにさし、火のほのくらき方にむかて、やはら、此刀をぬき出し、鬢にひきあてられけるが、氷などの樣にぞみえける。諸人目をすましけり。其上忠盛の郎等もとは一門たりし木工助平貞光が孫しんの三郎太夫家房が子、左兵衞尉家貞といふ者ありけり。薄青の狩衣の下に萠黄威の腹卷をき、弦袋つけたる太刀脇はさんで、殿上の小庭に畏てぞ候ける。貫首以下あやしみをなし、「うつぼ柱よりうち、鈴の綱のへんに布衣の者の候ふはなにものぞ。狼藉なり。罷出よ。」と、六位をもていはせければ、家貞申けるは「相傳の主、備前守殿今夜闇討にせられ給べき由承候あひだ、其ならむ樣を見むとて、かくて候。えこそ罷出まじけれ。」とて畏て候ければ、是等をよしなしとやおもはれけん、其夜の闇討なかりけり。

annotation.translation: However, when Tadamori was holding the post of Bizen-no-kami, he built and presented the Jōju-in Temple at the request of Emperor Toba, constructing a hall thirty-three ken long and installing 1,031 statues of the Buddha. The memorial service was held on the 13th day of the 3rd month of the first year of Tenjō. In reward, it was decreed that he should be granted a province he had previously lacked; thus, the province of Tajima was bestowed upon him. So moved was the retired emperor that he granted him permission to enter the inner palace. Tadamori was thirty-six years old when he entered the palace for the first time. Unkei, the Clouds Above, grew envious of this, and on the 23rd day of the 11th month of that same year, during the evening of the Five-Rites Feast of the Brightening, he plotted to ambush Tadamori in the dark. Tadamori, having heard of this, said, "I am not a scribe by birth; I was born into a family of warriors. Should I now, unexpectedly, suffer disgrace, it would be a matter of concern for the sake of my house and for my own sake. There is a fundamental principle that one must preserve one's life in order to serve one's lord." With this in mind, he made preparations in advance. At the very beginning of his entry into the inner palace, he wore a large scabbard with great dignity under his formal court robe, and as he approached the dimly lit area, he gently drew out this sword, bringing it to his hair, and it appeared like ice. All the people opened their eyes wide. Moreover, there was a man named Saitō no Jō no Tada, a grandson of the carpenter Taira no Tadahira (who had once belonged to the same clan as Tadamori's retainers), the son of Taira no Tadahiro, a left military attendant. He wore a light blue hunting robe with a mustard-yellow armored vest beneath it, a sword with a quiver attached, and a short sword at his side, standing respectfully in the small courtyard of the palace. The chief priest and others below were surprised, saying, "Why is a man in a cloth robe standing near the Utsubo pillar, pulling at the bell rope? This is a disturbance! Leave at once!" they commanded, ordering him to be expelled by virtue of his sixth rank. Tada replied respectfully, "While I have learned that the master of the house, Lord Bizen-no-kami, is to be ambushed in the dark tonight, I have come here to observe how it unfolds. I certainly cannot leave." Thus, they allowed this to happen, and the ambush that night did not take place.

text: 忠盛御前のめしにまはれければ、人々拍子をかへて「伊勢平氏はすがめなりけり。」とぞはやされける。此人々はかけまくもかたじけなく柏原天皇の御末とは申ながら、中比は都の住居もうと／＼しく、地下にのみ振舞なて伊勢國に住國ふかかりしかば、其國の器に事よせて、伊勢平氏とぞ申ける。其うへ忠盛目のすがまれたりければ、加樣にはやされけり。いかにすべき樣もなくして、御遊もいまだをはらざるに、竊に罷出らるとて、よこたへさされたりける刀をば紫宸殿の御後にして、かたへの殿上人のみられける所にて、主殿司をめしてあづけ置てぞ出られける。家貞待うけたてまつて、「さていかゞ候つる。」と申ければ、かくともいはまほしう思はれけれども、いひつるものならば、殿上までもやがてきりのぼらんずる者にてある間、「別の事もなし。」とぞ答られける。

annotation.translation: Because he was summoned to the presence of Lady Chūsei, the people changed their tune and said, "The Ise Taira clan is indeed a superior one." These people, though they deeply felt the gratitude of being in the line of Emperor Kashiwabara, yet the Nakahi held the capital's residence in disdain and served only the lower ranks, residing in the Ise Province. Therefore, they used the vessels of that province and came to be called the Ise Taira clan. Since Chūsei's eyes were truly superior, they were flattered by this. With no way to proceed and the imperial pleasures not yet concluded, he secretly left, taking a sword that had been laid across, placed it behind the Shishinden, and went out after entrusting it to the head of the Imperial Household Bureau. When Iesada received him and asked, "How have you been?", although he wished not to say this, since he was a person who would immediately ascend even to the upper chambers, he answered, "There is no other matter."

text: 五節には、「白薄樣、こぜむじの紙、卷上の筆、鞆繪ゑがいたる筆の軸」なんどさま％＼面白き事をのみこそうたひまはるるに、中比太宰權帥季仲卿といふ人ありけり。あまりに色のくろかりければ、見る人黒帥とぞ申ける。其人いまだ藏人頭なりし時、五節にまはれければ、それも拍子をかへて、「あなくろ／＼、くろき頭かな。いかなる人のうるしぬりけむ。」とぞはやされける。又花山院前太政大臣忠雅公、いまだ十歳と申し時、父中納言忠宗卿におくれたてまつて孤にておはしけるを、故中御門藤中納言家成卿いまだ播磨守たりし時、聟に執て、聲花にもてなされければ、それも五節に「播磨米はとくさか、むくの葉か、人のきらをみがくは。」とぞはやされける。上古には加樣にありしかども事いでこず。末代いかゞあらんずらむ、おぼつかなしとぞ人申ける。

annotation.translation: At the Five Festivals, things such as "white thin paper, ko-ze-muji paper, scrolls with brushwork from the top, and axes with Ega-itaru brushwork" were the sole subjects of songs, and there was a person named Nakahito Dazaikan Gonno Kami Suehara. Because his complexion was exceedingly dark, the people called him "Black General." When he was still Kurado no Kami, he participated in the Five Festivals, and the rhythm was changed: "Oh, so black, so black! What a black head! Whose lacquer painting has he become?" was chanted. Also, at the time when Emperor Hanazono, the former Daijo Daijin Taka-akira, was still ten years old, he was left an orphan by his father, the former Chunagon Tadamori, and when the late Fujiwara no Iesuke, who was still Harima no Kami, took him as a son-in-law and entertained him with the sounds of flowers, the Five Festivals also chanted: "Harima rice is harvested early, or the leaves of the muku tree, or one who polishes the people's sword." In ancient times, such things occurred often, but they did not happen in later generations. How could it be in the final ages? The people said, "It is uncertain."

text: 案のごとく五節はてにしかば、殿上人一同に申されけるは、「夫雄劍を帶して公宴に列し、兵仗を給て、宮中を出入するはみな格式の禮をまもる綸命よしある先規なり。しかるを忠盛朝臣或は相傳の郎從と號して布衣の兵を殿上の小庭にめしおき、或は腰の刀を横へさいて節繪の座につらなる。兩條希代いまだきかざる狼藉なり。事既に重疊せり。罪科尤ものがれがたし。早く御札をけづて闕官停任せらるべき由」おの／＼訴へ申されければ、上皇大に驚きおぼしめし、忠盛をめして御尋あり。陳じ申けるは、「まづ郎從小庭に祗候の由、全く覺悟つかまつらず。但し、近日人々あひたくまるゝ旨子細ある歟の間、年來の家人、事をつたへきくかによて其恥をたすけむが爲に、忠盛にしられずして竊に參候の條力及ざる次第なり。若し猶其咎あるべくば、彼身をめし進ずべき歟。次に刀の事、主殿司に預け置をはぬ。是をめし出され刀の實否について咎の左右あるべき歟。」と申。しかるべしとて、其刀をめし出して叡覽あれば、上は鞘卷のくろくぬりたりけるが、中は木刀に銀薄をぞおしたりける。「當座の恥辱をのがれん爲に刀を帶する由あらはすといへども、後日の訴訟を存知して、木刀を帶しける用意のほどこそ神妙なれ。弓箭に携らむ者のはかりごとは尤かうこそあらまほしけれ。兼ては又郎從小庭に祗候の條且は武士の郎等のならひなり。忠盛が咎にあらず。」とて却て叡感にあづかしうへは敢て罪科の沙汰もなかりけり。

annotation.translation: As anticipated, at the conclusion of the five sections, the nobles at court reported: 'It is a precedent established by imperial edict that all who attend public ceremonies with a sword at their side, receive weapons, and enter and exit the palace must strictly observe the prescribed ceremonial protocols. Yet, Taira no Tadamori, sometimes calling himself a hereditary attendant and placing a commoner's soldier in the inner court of the palace, and at other times wearing his sword sideways while sitting in a seat decorated with seasonal paintings, commits an unprecedented scandal that has never before been heard of in the capital. The matter has already become serious and grave. The offense is particularly heinous and difficult to overlook. We urgently request that an imperial edict be issued to suspend his office.' They each petitioned in this manner. The Retired Emperor was greatly startled and ordered Tadamori to be summoned. Tadamori explained: 'First, I did not fully prepare myself to attend the inner court as a junior attendant. However, hearing that people wished to meet soon, and wishing to protect the honor of my long-serving household by passing on matters through them, I secretly entered the palace without Tadamori's knowledge, but I was unable to fulfill my duties. If there is still any blame to be found, I am willing to offer my own life as a sacrifice. Regarding the sword matter, I did not entrust it to the Chief Chamberlain. If this is presented for examination, there may be grounds for either guilt or innocence.' This was the account. It seemed appropriate, so the sword was presented for the Emperor's inspection. The outer layer of the scabbard was black-lacquered, but inside was a wooden sword plated with thin silver. 'Although he claims to wear a sword to avoid the shame of this moment, knowing full well that legal proceedings would follow later, his preparation of wearing a wooden sword is truly extraordinary. Those who carry bows and arrows should indeed take such measures. Furthermore, it is customary for warriors to serve as junior attendants in the inner court. Thus, Tadamori bears no guilt.' Consequently, the Emperor was deeply moved, and no further punishment was meted out.

text: とよみたりければ、いとゞあさからずぞおもはれける。薩摩守忠度の母、是なり。にるを友とかやの風情に忠盛もすいたりければ、かの女房も優なりけり。かくて忠盛刑部卿になて、仁平三年正月十五日歳五十八にてうせにき。清盛嫡男たるによてその迹をつぐ。

annotation.translation: Since he had heard of her, he thought even less of her. She was the mother of Satsuma-no-mori Tadanori. Because Tadamori had also made Niro his friend with the same kind of sentiment, that lady was also excellent. Thus, Tadamori became Shibu-sho, and at the age of fifty-eight on the 15th day of the first month of the third year of Ninpei, he died. text: 保元々年七月に宇治の左府代をみだり給し時、安藝守とて御方にて勳功ありしかば、播磨守にうつて同三年太宰大貳になる。次に平治元年十二月、信頼卿が謀反の時、御方にて賊徒をうちたひらげ、勳功一にあらず、恩賞是おもかるべしとて、次の年正三位に敍せられ、うちつゞき、宰相、衞府督、檢非違使別當、中納言、大納言に歴あがて、剰へ丞相の位にいたり、左右を歴ずして内大臣より太政大臣從一位にあがる。大將にあらね共、兵仗をたまはて隨身をめし具す。牛車輦車の宣旨を蒙て、のりながら宮中を出入す。偏に執政の臣のごとし。「太政大臣は一人に師範として四海に儀刑せり。國を治め、道を論じ、陰陽をやはらげをさむ。其人にあらずば即ち闕けよ。」といへり。されば則闕の官とも名付たり。其人ならではけがすべき官ならねども、一天四海を掌の内ににぎられしうへは子細に及ばず。

annotation.translation: In the seventh month of the first year of Hogen, when the Left Minister at Uji was arbitrarily relieved of his post, since he was an Aide of Awa Province, a man of the imperial side, and had meritorious achievements, he was transferred to the position of Aide of Harima and became Dazai no Daifu in the same third year. Next, in the twelfth month of the first year of Heiji, at the time of the rebellion of the Minister Shinnobu, as a man of the imperial side he defeated the rebels, and since his meritorious achievements were not limited to one, his rewards should be considered, in the following year he was elevated to the Third Rank, and continuously he ascended through the positions of Chancellor, Director of the Guard, Deputy Chief of the Non-Official Affairs, Junior Counselor, Senior Counselor, and ultimately reached the position of Chancellor, serving in both the Left and Right, and rising from the Minister of the Left to the Grand Minister of State, the First Rank with the Junior Rank. Although he was not a General, he was granted weapons and ordered to be attended by his personal guards. He received an imperial edict for a carriage and sedan chair, and while riding it he entered and exited the imperial palace. He was exactly like a minister who held executive power. 'The Grand Minister of State serves as a model for one and sets an example for the four seas. He governs the country, discusses the Way, and moderates the Yin and Yang. If there is no such person, then the post should be left vacant.' Thus it was said. Therefore, even the vacant office was named 'the Vacant Office.' Although it is not an office that should be defiled by anyone other than such a person, when one who holds the entire four seas in the palm of his hand is in charge, there is no need for detailed consideration.

text: 平家かやうに繁昌せられけるも熊野權現の御利生とぞきこえし。其故は、古へ清盛公、いまだ安藝守たりし時、伊勢の海より船にて熊野へまゐられけるに、大きなる鱸の船にをどり入たりけるを、先達申けるは、「是は權現の御利生なり。いそぎまゐるべし。」と申ければ、清盛のたまひけるは、「昔、周の武王の船にこそ白魚は躍入たりけるなれ。是吉事なり。」とて、さばかり十戒をたもちて、精進潔齋の道なれども、調味して家の子、侍ともにくはせられけり。其故にや吉事のみうちつゞいて太政大臣まできはめ給へり。子孫の官途も龍の雲に上るよりは猶すみやかなり。九代の先蹤をこえ給ふこそ目出けれ。

annotation.translation: That the Taira clan flourished thus was reported as the benefit of the Kumano Gongen. The reason is that in ancient times, when Lord Kiyomori was still the Governor of Awa, he boarded a ship from the sea of Ise to go to Kumano, where he saw a large boat of perch leaping in. The guide said, 'This is the benefit of the Gongen. You should hasten your journey.' Kiyomori then said, 'In the past, it was only when the boat of King Wu of Zhou that white fish leaped in; this is a fortunate omen.' Although he strictly observed the Ten Precepts and the path of asceticism and purity, he had seasoned food served to his household children and retainers. Because of this, perhaps only fortunate events continued, and he reached the position of Daijō-daijin. Even the official careers of his descendants are more splendid than ascending on the dragon's clouds. To surpass the nine generations of ancestors is truly auspicious.

text: 角て清盛公、仁安三年十一月十一日歳五十一にて病にをかされ、存命の爲に忽に出家入道す。法名は淨海とこそなのられけれ。其しるしにや、宿病たちどころにいえて、天命を全す。人のしたがひつく事吹風の草木をなびかすがごとし。世のあまねく仰げる事ふる雨の國土をうるほすに同じ。

annotation.translation: The Kado no Taira no Kiyomori, on the eleventh day of the eleventh month of the third year of Nin'an, at the age of fifty-one, was seized by illness; yet, in order to preserve his life, he suddenly became a monk and entered the priesthood. His Dharma name was said to be Jōkai. As evidence of this, his chronic illness was immediately cured, and he fulfilled his heavenly mandate. To follow one's lord is like the grasses and trees bending to the blowing wind. To be universally revered by the world is like the long-rain that moistens the lands.

text:
六波羅殿の御一家の君達といひてしかば、花族も英雄も面をむかへ肩をならぶる
人なし。されば入道相國のこしうと、平大納言時忠卿ののたまひけるは「此一門にあ
らざらむ人は皆人非人なるべし。」とぞのたまひける。かゝりしかば、いかなる人も
相構へて其ゆかりにむすぼほれんとぞしける。衣文のかきやう烏帽子のため樣よりは
じめて何事も六波羅樣といひてければ、一天四海の人皆是をまなぶ。

annotation.translation: Since they were referred to as the lords of the Rokuhara mansion, there was no one, whether from the noble clans or among the heroes, who did not turn their faces toward them and stand shoulder to shoulder. Therefore, the statement made by the retired imperial prince and the Great Counselor, Prince Tokitada, was: 'Anyone who is not of this house must be a non-human.' Thus, no matter who they were, they all sought to associate themselves with that lineage. Whether it was the style of dressing in robes or the style of the cap, and indeed everything, was referred to as 'the Rokuhara style,' and people throughout the entire land and the four seas learned from this.

text:
又いかなる賢王聖主の御政も攝政關白の御成敗も世にあまされたるいたづら者な
どの、人のきかぬ處にてなにとなうそしり傾け申事は常の習なれども、此禪門世ざか
りの程は聊いるかせにも申者なし。其故は入道相國のはかりごとに十四五六の童部を
三百人そろへて、髮をかぶろにきりまはし、あかき直垂をきせて、めしつかはれける
が、京中にみち／＼て、往反しけり。自ら平家の事あしざまに申者あれば、一人きゝ
出さぬほどこそありけれ、餘黨に觸廻して、其家に亂入し資材雜具を追捕し、其奴を
搦とて、六波羅へゐてまゐる。されば目に見、心に知るといへども、詞にあらはれて
申者なし。六波羅殿の禿と云ひてしかば、道をすぐる馬車もよぎてぞ、通りける。禁
門を出入すといへども姓名を尋らるゝに及ばず、京師の長吏これが為に目を側むとみ
えたり。

annotation.translation: Moreover, while it is the common custom for foolish people who are widely known in the world to slander and accuse without any cause in places where people cannot hear, in the case of this Zenmon during the time when the world was in disorder, there was not even a whisper of such slander. The reason is that the Insei Daimyo gathered thirty children of fourteen, fifteen, and sixteen years of age, dressed them in head coverings, clad them in red hitatare, and sent them to serve. They filled the capital, moving back and forth. Since there was a certain improper statement about the Taira clan, one who heard it would not remain silent, and they would turn to the remaining forces, break into their houses, pursue and seize their property and miscellaneous tools, seize these slaves, and bring them to Rokuhara. Therefore, although they saw it with their eyes and knew it in their hearts, there was no one who expressed it in words. Because they were called 'the tonsured ones of the Rokuhara Palace,' even the horse-drawn carriages passing by would make way and pass. Even though they entered and exited the Forbidden Gate, they did not even need to inquire about their names; it appeared that the high officials of the capital turned their eyes away because of this.

text:
吾身の榮花を極るのみならず、一門共に繁昌して、嫡子重盛、内大臣の左大將、次男宗盛、中納言の右大將、三男知盛、三位中將、嫡孫維盛、四位少將、すべて一門
の公卿十六人、殿上人三十餘人、諸國の受領、衞府、諸司、都合六十餘人なり。世にはまた人なくぞ見えられける。

annotation.translation: Not only did we bring our own prosperity to its peak, but the entire clan flourished together: the legitimate heir Shigemori, Left Great General and Minister of the Interior; the second son Munemori, Right Great General and Middle Counselor; the third son Tomomori, Junior Counselor of the Third Rank; the legitimate grandson Koremori, Junior General of the Fourth Rank; in all, sixteen members of the clan served as high-ranking nobles, and over thirty others served as courtiers; governors of the various provinces, heads of the Guard Offices, and officials of the various bureaus totaled over sixty. Such a state of affairs had never been seen in the world.

text:
昔奈良の御門の御時、神龜五年、朝家に中衞の大將をはじめおかれ、大同四年に
中衞を近衞と改られしよりこのかた、兄弟左右に相並事僅に三四箇度なり。文徳天皇
の御時は左に良房右大臣左大將、右に良相、大納言の右大將、是は閑院の左大臣冬嗣
の御子なり。朱雀院の御宇には左に實頼、小野宮殿、右に師輔、九條殿、貞信公の御
子なり。御冷泉院の御時は、左に教通、大二條殿、右に頼宗、堀河殿、御堂の關白の
御子なり。二條院の御宇には左に基房、松殿、右に兼實、月輪殿、法性寺殿の御子な
り。是皆攝祿の臣の御子息、凡人にとりては其例なし。殿上
の交をだにきらはれし人の子孫にて禁色雜袍をゆり、綾羅錦繍を身にまとひ、大臣大
將になて、兄弟、左右に相並事、末代とはいひながら不思議なりし事どもなり。

annotation.translation: In ancient times, during the reign of the Imperial Gate of Nara, in the fifth year of Jingi, he was appointed as the Captain of the Middle Guard beginning from the Court House; since the Middle Guard was renamed the Close Guard in the fourth year of Daidō, it has happened only three or four times that brothers have stood side by side on the left and right. During the reign of Emperor Montoku, on the left was Yoshifusa, Minister of the Left and Captain of the Left, and on the right was Yoshisuke, Vice-Minister of the Right and Captain of the Right; the latter was the son of Tōtsuji, Minister of the Left of Kan-in. During the reign of Emperor Suzaku, on the left was Sanetoy, of the Minor Palace, and on the right was Morisuke, of the Ninth Street, who was the son of the Lord Teishin. During the reign of Emperor Reizei, on the left was Michimichi, of the Second Dai-Niō, and on the right was Yorimune, of Horikawa, who was the son of the Regent of the Temple of the Hall. During the reign of the Second Temple, on the left was Motofusa, of Shōden, and on the right was Kanenari, of Gesshin, who was the son of the Lord of Hōjō-ji. All of these were sons of ministers who held both regency and power; for ordinary people, such an example does not exist. The descendants of those who were even permitted to participate in courtly gatherings, wearing the forbidden colors and mixed robes, donning silk and brocade, rising to the positions of Minister and Captain, with brothers standing side by side on the left and right—though this is said to be in the distant age, it is indeed a remarkable occurrence.

其外御娘八人おはしき。皆とり／＼に幸給へり。一人は櫻町の中納言重教卿の北
の方にておはすべかりしが、八歳の時約束ばかりにて平治の亂以後ひきちがへられ、
花山院の左大臣殿の御臺盤所にならせ給て君達あまたましましけり。

annotation.translation: Besides them, there were eight noble daughters. They were all blessed with happiness in various ways. One was destined to become the wife of Lord Shigemichi, the Middle Counsellor of the Sakuramachi clan, but when she was eight years old, after the Heiji Rebellion, she was separated from him merely by a promise, and she was made a lady-in-waiting to the Minister of the Left of the Hanazono-in, where many noble ladies served her.

text: 抑この重教卿を櫻町の中納言と申ける事はすぐれて心數奇給へる人にて、つねは吉野山をこひ、町に櫻をうゑならべ、其内に屋を立て、すみたまひしかば、來る年の春ごとに、みる人櫻町とぞ申ける。櫻はさいて七箇日にちるを、名殘を惜み天照御神に祈申されければ、三七日迄名殘ありけり。君も賢王にてましませば神も神徳を輝かし、花も心ありければ、二十日の齡をたもちけり。

annotation.translation: Indeed, this Kiyotaka, the Middle Counselor of Sakuramachi, was a person of remarkable eccentricity; he always longed for Yoshino Mountain, planted cherry trees in rows in the town, built a house within them, and resided there. Thus, every spring of the following year, the people who came to see the blossoms called him 'Sakuramachi.' Since the cherry blossoms normally fall after seven days, he prayed to Amaterasu Omikami to cherish their lingering beauty, and thus the remnants remained for thirty-seven days. As the Emperor was also a wise king, the gods also shone with divine virtue, and the flowers possessed a heart, so he maintained them for twenty days.

text: 一人は后にたゝせ給ふ。王子御誕生ありて皇太子に立ち、位につかせ給しかば、院號かうぶらせ給ひて、建禮門院とぞ申ける。入道相國の御娘なるうへ、天下の國母にてましましければとかう申におよばず。一人は六條の攝政殿の北政所にならせ給ふ。高倉院御在位の時御母代とて准三后の宣旨をかうぶり、白河殿とておもき人にてましましけり。一人は普賢寺殿の北の政所にならせ給ふ。一人は冷泉大納言隆房卿の北方。一人は七條修理大夫信隆卿に相具し給へり。又安藝國嚴島の内侍が腹に一人おはせしは、後白河の法皇へまゐらせたまひて女御のやうにてぞましましける。其外九條院の雜仕常葉が腹に一人。これは花山院殿に上臈女房にて廊の御方とぞ申ける。

annotation.translation: One was appointed consort to the Emperor. When the Prince was born and became Crown Prince and was given a post, he was bestowed the temple name and was called Dairi Taimen-in. As the daughter of the Retired Emperor and Minister of the Right, and since she was the Mother of the Nation for the whole realm, it was not appropriate to call her by that name. One was made the North Chamberlain of the Regent's residence at Rokujō. During the reign of Emperor Takakura, she was honored with the title of准Emperor and was called Shira-kawa-dono, a very important person. One was made the North Chamberlain of the residence of the temple of Fugen-ji. One was the North Chamberlain of Prince Takafusa, Dainagon of the Saionji clan. One was made the consort of Nobutaka, Shuri-no-daibu of the Shichijō clan. Furthermore, one was born to the lady-in-waiting of Itsukushima in Awa Province; she was sent to Emperor Go-Shirakawa and lived like a female consort. Another one was born to the lady-in-waiting Tokiba, an attendant of the Kujō-in. This one was appointed as a senior lady-in-waiting to Prince Hanazono and was called the lady of the corridor.

One was made the North Chamberlain of the Regent's residence at Rokujō. During the reign of Emperor Takakura, she was honored with the title of准Emperor and was called Shira-kawa-dono, a very important person. text: 日本秋津島は纔に六十六箇國、平家知行の國三十餘箇國、既に半國にこえたり。其外莊園田畠いくらといふ數をしらず。綺羅充滿して、堂上花の如し。軒騎群集して門前市をなす。楊州の金、荊州の珠、呉郡の綾、蜀江の錦、七珍萬寶一として闕たる事なし。歌堂舞閣の基、魚龍爵馬の翫物、恐らくは帝闕も仙洞も是にはすぎじとぞ見えし。

annotation.translation: The land of Japan, the Autumn-Spring Island, consists of merely sixty-six provinces; the provinces under the Heike clan's control number more than thirty, already exceeding half of the country. As for the number of manors and rice fields outside of these, it is unknown. They are filled with glittering splendor, like flowers in the imperial court. Crowds of riders gather, making a market before the gates. The gold of Yangzhou, the pearls of Jingzhou, the silk of Wujun, and the brocade of the Shu River—there is not a single one of the seven treasures and ten thousand treasures that is lacking. The foundation of singing halls and dancing pavilions, the playthings of fish, dragons, nobles, and horses—truly, even the imperial palace and the retired emperor's residence must appear to be surpassed by this.

text: 入道相國、一天四海をたなごゝろのうちににぎりたまひし間、世のそしりをもはばからず、人の嘲りをもかへり見ず、不思議の事をのみし給へり。たとへば其比都に聞えたる白拍子の上手、祇王祇女とて兄弟あり、とぢといふ白拍子が娘なり。姉の祇王を入道相國最愛せられければ、是によて妹の祇女をも世の人もてなす事なのめならず。母とぢにもよき屋つくてとらせ、毎月百石百貫をおくられければ、家内富貴してたのしい事なのめならず。

annotation.translation: While the monk-statesman, who had the entire world in the palm of his hand, did not fear the world's slander, nor did he look back at people's mockery, he did only the extraordinary. For instance, there was a famous female dancer named Shirabyōshi heard of in the capital at that time, who had a brother and sister named Giō and Gijō, and Gijō was the daughter of the dancer Toji. Since the monk-statesman loved the elder sister Giō the most, it was not strange that people of the world also treated the younger sister Gijō with favor. Toji, the mother, was also given a fine house, and every month one hundred koku and one hundred kan were sent to them, so that their household was wealthy and the situation was not strange at all.

text: 抑我朝に白拍子のはじまりける事は、昔鳥羽院の御宇に島の千歳和歌の前とてこれら二人がまひいだしたりけるなり。始めは水干に立烏帽子、白鞘卷をさいて、舞ひければ、男舞とぞ申ける。然るを中比より烏帽子、刀をのけられ、水干ばかりをもちゐたり、さてこそ白拍子とは名付けれ。

annotation.translation: As for the beginning of the profession of biwa-playing women in our country, it was that during the reign of Emperor Toba, two individuals, Shima no Chitose and Waka, danced together. At first, they wore water-dyed robes, black court hats, and white-sheathed sword wraps, and when they danced, they were called 'male dances.' However, from the middle Heian period, they were ordered to remove the black court hats and swords, and wearing only the water-dyed robes, it was then that they came to be named 'biwa-playing women.'

text: 京中の白拍子ども祇王が幸の目出度きやうをきいてうらやむ者もあり、そねむ者もありけり。羨む者共は「あなめでたの祇王御前が幸や。おなじあそび女とならば、誰もみなあの樣でこそありたけれ。いかさま是は祇といふ文字を名についてかくはめでたきやらん。いざ我等もついて見む。」とて或は祇一と付き、祇二と付き、或は祗福祗徳などいふ者も有けり。そねむ者どもは「なん條名により、文字にはよるべき。幸はたゞ前世の生れつきにてこそあんなれ。」とてつかぬ者もおほかりけり。

annotation.translation: Among the people of Kyoto, there were those who envied the fortunate days of the white-robed dancer Gikō, and there were also those who resented her. The envious ones said, "Ah, how admirable is Gikō's good fortune! If we are to be courtesans, surely everyone should be like her. Truly, how admirable it must be to bear the character 'Gi' in one's name. Let us go and see her." Thus, some followed her as 'Gichi,' others as 'Gini,' and some even took names such as 'Gifuku' or 'Gitoku.' As for those who resented her, they said, "Names are merely arbitrary; one should not rely on them. Good fortune is solely a matter of one's birth in a previous life." Consequently, there were many who held such foolish thoughts.

text: かくて三年と申に又都にきこえたる白拍子の上手一人出來たり。加賀國のものなり。名をば佛とぞ申ける。年十六とぞきこえし。「昔よりおほくの白拍子ありしかども、かかる舞は、いまだ見ず。」とて京中の上下もてなす事なのめならず。佛御前申けるは「我天下に聞えたれども、當時さしもめでたうさかえさせ給ふ平家太政の入道殿へめされぬ事こそ本意なけれ。あそびもののならひ、なにかはくるしかるべき。推參して見む。」とて、ある時西八條へぞまゐりたる。人まゐて「當時都にきこえ候佛御前こそまゐて候へ。」と申しければ、入道「なんでうさやうのあそびものは人の召に隨てこそ參れ。左右なう推參する樣やある。祇王があらん處へは神ともいへ、佛ともいへ、かなふまじきぞ。とう／＼罷出よ。」とぞの給ひける。佛御前はすげなういはれたてまつて、已にいでんとしけるを、祇王、入道殿に申けるは「あそび者の推參は常の習でこそ候へ。其上、年もいまだをさなう候ふなるが、たま／＼思たてまゐりて候を、すげなう仰られてかへさせ給はん事こそ不便なれ。いかばかりはづかしうかたはらいたくも候ふらむ。わがたてし道なれば、人の上ともおぼえず。たとひ舞を御覽じ、歌をきこしめさずとも、御對面ばかりさぶらうてかへさせ給ひたらば、ありがたき御情でこそ候はんずれ。たゞ理をまげて、めしかへして御對面さぶらへ。」と申ければ、入道、「いで／＼、我御前があまりにいふ事なれば、見參してかへさむ。」とてつかひを立てぞめされける。佛御前はすげなういはれたてまつて車に乘て既にいでんとしけるが、めされて歸參りたり。入道出あひ對面して「今日の見參はあるまじかりつるを、祇王が何と思ふやらん、餘りに申しすゝむる間、か樣に見參しつ。見參する程にてはいかで聲をもきかであるべきぞ。今樣一つうたへかし。」とのたまへば、佛御前「承りさぶらふ。」とて今樣一つぞ歌うたる。

annotation.translation: Thus, it was reported to the capital after three years that a skilled female dancer and singer had appeared. She was from Kaga Province. Her name was Hotoke, so they said. She was said to be sixteen years old. "There have been many female dancers and singers since ancient times, but I have never yet seen a dance like this," they said, and the people of all ranks in Kyoto tried to entertain her. Hotoke, in her address to the Lord, said, "Although I have heard my name throughout the realm, my true wish is that I have not been summoned by the great monk Dajō Dainagon of the Heike family, whose fame and glory shone so brilliantly at that time. As one who follows the ways of entertainment, surely I should come when summoned. I will push my way forward and go see him." And so, at one time, she went to the residence of Nishi-Hachijō. A servant came and said, "The Lady Hotoke, whose name was widely known in the capital, should now come." The monk replied, "Why should one who engages in such amusements come simply because summoned by another? There is no need to push one's way forward. Wherever Gionō may be, whether it be a god or a Buddha, one cannot go there. Leave at once!" Thus he commanded. Hotoke, having been spoken to very harshly, was about to depart, but Gionō said to the Lord, "It is customary for entertainers to push their way forward when summoned. Moreover, she is still quite young, and although she has been summoned from time to time, to be spoken to so harshly and sent back would be inconvenient. How embarrassed and distressed she must be feeling! Since it is my own path, I feel no hesitation. Even if you do not wish to see her dance or hear her sing, if you would merely grant her an audience and then send her back, that would indeed be a gracious disposition. Just bend the rules slightly, summon her back, and allow her to have an audience." When she said this, the Lord replied, "Very well, since this Lady has spoken so strongly, I will summon her and let her go." And so he sent a messenger to summon her. Hotoke, having been spoken to very harshly, had already mounted her carriage and was about to depart, but was summoned and returned. The Lord came out to meet her and have an audience, saying, "I was not going to grant an audience today, but what could Gionō think? Because she pleaded so earnestly, I came to grant an audience. But to grant an audience is not enough to hear her voice. Now, please sing a single song." Upon this command, Hotoke replied, "I shall comply," and so she sang a single song.

text: とおし返し／＼三返歌すましたりければ、見聞の人々みな耳目をおどろかす。入道もおもしろげに思ひ給ひて、「我御前は今樣は上手でありけるよ。此定では舞も定めてよかるらん。一番見ばや。鼓打めせ。」とてめされけり。うたせて一番舞たりけり。

annotation.translation: After passing back and forth three times the song, which had been completed, all the people of experience and observation were amazed. The Cloistered Emperor thought it delightful, saying, 'Myself in the past was skilled in this manner. In this fixed form, even the dance would surely be proper. Let us see the first one. Beat the drum.' And thus he commanded. He was made to sing, and he danced the first dance.

text: 佛御前は髮姿よりはじめてみめ形うつくしく聲よく節も上手でありければ、なじかは舞もそんずべき。心も及ばず舞すましたりければ、入道相國舞にめで給ひて佛に心をうつされけり。佛御前「こはされば何事さぶらふぞや。もとよりわらはは、推參の者にていだされまゐらせさぶらひしを、祇王御前の申状によてこそ召返されても候に、加樣にめしおかれなば、祇王御前の思ひ給はん心のうちはづかしうさぶらふ。はや／＼暇をたうで出させおはしませ。」と申ければ、入道、「すべて其儀あるまじ。但祇王があるをはゞかるか。其儀ならば祇王をこそいださめ。」と宣ひける。佛御前「それ又いかでかさる御事候べき。諸共にめしおかれんだに心うう候べきに、まして祇王御前を出させ給ひて、わらは一人めしおかれなば、祇王御前の心のうちはづかしう候ふべし。おのづから後までわすれぬ御事ならば、めされて又は參るとも、今日は暇を給らむ。」とぞ申ける。入道「なんでう其儀あるべき。祇王とう／＼罷出でよ。」と御使かさねて三度までこそ立てられけれ。祇王もとよりおもひ設けたる道なれども、さすがに昨日今日とは思よらず。いそぎ出べき由頻にのたまふ間、はき拭ひ、塵ひろはせ、見苦しき物共とりしたためて出づべきにこそ定まりけれ。一樹の陰に宿り合ひ、同じ流をむすぶだに別はかなしき習ぞかし。まして此三年が間住なれし處なれば、名殘もをしう悲しくて、かひなき涙ぞこぼれける。さてもあるべき事ならねば、祇王すでに、今はかうとて、出けるが、なからん跡の忘れ形見にもとや思ひけむ、障子になく／＼一首の歌をぞかきつけける。

annotation.translation: Buddha Gozen, from the very beginning of her appearance as a hairdresser, was beautiful in form and voice, and skilled in rhythm, so surely she could perform the dance. Since she also danced with a graceful heart, the Cloistered Retired Emperor greatly rejoiced in the dance and had his heart captured by Buddha Gozen. Buddha Gozen said, "Since this is so, what business do you have here? Originally, I was summoned as a servant of the Tenth Rank and have been serving there; I would have returned only upon the petition of Giō Gozen. If you were to command me to stay as well, I would feel deeply ashamed of Giō Gozen's feelings. Please, quickly grant me leave and let me depart." Upon hearing this, the Cloistered Retired Emperor said, "There must be no such thing. But is it because you are worried about Giō Gozen? If that is the case, then let Giō Gozen depart as well." Buddha Gozen said, "How could that be? Even if all of us were to be kept here, my heart would be troubled; how much more so if you were to send Giō Gozen away and keep me alone, for I would feel deeply ashamed of Giō Gozen's feelings. If it is a matter that will be remembered until the end, then even if I am summoned again later, please grant me leave today." Thus she spoke. The Cloistered Retired Emperor said, "Why would there be such a matter? Giō Gozen, please depart." The messenger was sent repeatedly, and she was urged three times. Although Giō Gozen had originally planned this path, she did not think it would happen so soon, yesterday or today. As the Emperor repeatedly commanded her to depart quickly, she wiped her tears, swept up the dust, and gathered her humble belongings to prepare to leave, and it was decided that she should depart. Even under the shade of a single tree, to share a lodging and even to join the same stream is a sorrowful habit. Moreover, since she had lived there for these three years, her lingering feelings were so sorrowful and sad that futile tears fell. Yet, since this was not an inevitable event, Giō Gozen, now having departed in this manner, perhaps thought of her departure as a memento of what had been; thus she wrote a single poem upon the sliding door.

text: さて車に乘て宿所に歸り、障子の内に倒れ臥し、唯泣くより外の事ぞき。母や妹是をみて「如何にやいかに。」ととひけれども、とかうの返事にも及ばず。具したる女に尋ねてぞさる事ありともしりてける。さる程に毎月に送られつる百石百貫をも今はとゞめられて、佛御前がゆかりの者共ぞ、始めて、樂み榮えける。京中の上下、「祇王こそ入道殿よりいとま給はて出でたんなれ。いざ見參して遊ばむ。」とて、或は文をつかはす人もあり、或は使を立つる者もあり。祇王さればとて今更人に對面してあそびたはぶるべきにもあらねば、文を取入るゝ事もなく、まして使にあひしらふ迄もなかりけり。是につけても悲しくていとゞ涙にのみぞしづみける。

annotation.translation: Well, she boarded the carriage, returned to her lodging, collapsed inside the shoji screen, and there was nothing to do but weep. Her mother and sister, seeing this, asked, 'What shall we do? What shall we do?' but she did not even reply. It was only after she learned from a well-informed woman that such a thing had happened that she came to know. At that time, the hundred koku and one hundred kan that had been sent to her every month were now withheld, and those who had some connection with the Buddha's altar were, for the first time, rejoicing and flourishing. People throughout Kyoto, high and low, said, 'Since Giō has been dismissed by the Daisōzu, let us go and see her.' Some sent letters, while others dispatched messengers. But since Giō was now in such a state that she could not meet with people or socialize even at this late stage, she did not even accept any letters, let alone receive or speak with any messengers. On top of all this, she was filled with sorrow and sank even deeper into tears.

text: かくて今年も暮れぬ。あくる春の比、入道相國、祇王が許へ使者を立てて、「いかに其後何事かある。佛御前があまりにつれ／＼げに見ゆるに、まゐて今樣をもうたひ、舞などをも舞て佛なぐさめよ。」とぞ宣ひける。祇王とかうの御返事にも及ばず。入道「など祇王は返事はせぬぞ。參るまじいか。參るまじくば、其樣を申せ。淨海もはからふ旨あり。」とぞ宣ひける。母とぢ是を聞くにかなしくて、[1]いかなるべしともおぼえす、なく／＼教訓しけるは、「いかに祇王御前、ともかくも御返事を申せかし、さやうにしかられ參らせんよりは。」といへば、祇王「參らんとおもふ道ならばこそやがて參るとも申さめ。參らざらんもの故に何と御返事を申すべしともおぼえず。此度めさんに參らずばはからふ旨ありと仰せらるゝは、都の外へ出さるゝか、さらずば命を召さるゝか、是二つによも過ぎじ。縱都を出さるゝとも、歎くべきにあらず。たとひ命を召さるゝとも、惜かるべき又わが身かは。一度憂きものに思はれ參らせて二度面をむかふべきにもあらず。」とて、なほ御返事をも申さゞりけるを、母とぢ重ねて教訓しけるは、「天が下に住ん程はともかうも入道殿の仰をば背くまじき事にてあるぞ。男女の縁宿世今にはじめぬ事ぞかし。千年萬年と契れども、軈て離るゝ中もあり。白地とは思へどもながらへ果る事もあり。世に定なきものは男女の習なり。それに我御前は此三年まで思はれまゐらせたれば、ありがたき御情でこそあれ。めさんに參らねばとて命をうしなはるゝまではよもあらじ。唯都の外へぞ出されんずらん。縱ひ都を出さるとも、我御前たちは年若ければ、如何ならん岩木のはざまにても過さん事安かるべし。年老い衰へたる母都の外へぞ出されんずらん。習はぬ旅の住居こそかねて思ふも悲しけれ。唯我を都の内にて住果させよ。其ぞ今生後生の孝養と思はむずる。」といへば、祇王うしと思し道なれども、親の命を背かじと、なく／＼又出立ける心の中こそ無慚なれ。一人參らむはあまりにものうしとて妹の祇女をも相具しけり。其外白拍子二人、惣じて四人一車に乘て、西八條へぞ參たる。さき／＼召されたる處へはいれられずして、遙に下りたる處に座敷しつらうて置かれたり。祇王「こは、されば、何事ぞや。我身に過つ事は無けれども、すてられたてまつるだにあるに、座敷をさへ下げらるゝ事の心うさよ。いかにせむ。」と思ふに、知らせじと押ふる袖のひまよりも餘りて涙ぞこぼれける。佛御前是を見て、あまりにあはれに思ければ、「あれはいかに、日頃召されぬ所にても候はばこそ。是へ召され候へかし。さらずばわらはに暇を給べ。出でて見參せん。」と申ければ、入道「すべて其儀あるまじ。」と宣ふ間、力及ばで出でざりけり。其後入道は祇王が心の内をも知たまはず、「いかに其後何事かある。さては佛御前があまりにつれ／＼げに見ゆるに、今樣一つ歌へかし。」とのたまへば、祇王參る程では、ともかうも入道殿の仰をば背くまじと思ひければ、落つる涙をおさへて、今樣一つぞ歌うたる。

annotation.translation: Thus, the year also draws to a close. When the following spring arrived, the Cloistered Prince sent an envoy to Giō's quarters, saying, 'What has happened since? Because Buddha's Lady appears so excessively sorrowful and dejected, come now and recite a poem of the present day, dance, and so on, to comfort Buddha.' This was what he declared. Giō could not offer any such reply. The Cloistered Prince said, 'Why does Giō not reply? She should not come. If she is not coming, then state that. Jinkai also has something in mind.' He declared thus. Her mother, hearing this, found it unbearable, [1] thinking she could not decide what to do, and repeatedly urged her, saying, 'How can Buddha's Lady not, in any case, give a reply? Rather than being treated in such a manner, she should comply.' Giō replied, 'If I intended to go, I would have said so immediately. Since I do not intend to go, I do not know what reply to give. If they say that I should not come and that Jinkai has something in mind, it must mean either that I will be expelled from the capital or that my life will be taken; there is no way it could be anything else. Even if I am expelled from the capital, there is nothing to lament. Even if my life is taken, is there anything worth mourning in my own body? There is no need to be treated as a sorrowful person once and then to meet with my face again.' Thus, she did not offer any reply. Her mother, urging her again, said, 'While living under Heaven, one must never go against the Cloistered Lord's command. The bond between man and woman is not begun only now. Even if one promises for a thousand or ten thousand years, there are times when they must part. Even if the cloth is white, there are times when it wears out completely. The impermanence of the world is the nature of men and women. Because Buddha's Lady has been cherished by him for these three years, this is a precious affection. It is not that she will lose her life for not coming; rather, she will simply be expelled from the capital. Even if she is expelled from the capital, if Buddha's Lady is young, she can surely survive even in the rocky passes of Mount Iwaki. But my aging, declining mother will be expelled from the capital. A residence in a journey one has not practiced is indeed sorrowful to contemplate beforehand. Just let me live out my days within the capital. This is what I shall consider as filial piety in this life and the next.' Saying this, although Giō thought it painful, she could not go against her parent's command, and with tears in her eyes, her heart was filled with shame as she resolved to depart. She took her sister, Giōjo, with her, as going alone was too burdensome. Two other female performers joined them, making four in total, who rode in a single carriage to Nishi-Hachijō. They could not enter the place where they had been summoned before; instead, a room had been prepared far below. Giō thought, 'This is it; what is this? I have done no wrong, yet I am abandoned, and even my room is lowered. How can this not be a source of sorrow?' As she pondered this, more tears flowed than could be held back by the sleeve that tried to suppress them. Buddha's Lady, seeing this, thought it too pitiful and said, 'Why is she here? If she had been summoned to a place she usually does not visit, that would be fine. Summon her here. If not, grant me permission to go out and see her.' While the Cloistered Prince was saying, 'There must be no such thing,' she was unable to go out due to lack of strength. Later, the Cloistered Prince, unaware of Giō's inner thoughts, said, 'What has happened since? Now that Buddha's Lady appears so excessively sorrowful, recite a single poem of the present day.' Giō, thinking that she could not go against the Cloistered Lord's command, even in the slightest, suppressed her falling tears and sang a single poem of the present day.

text: と泣く／＼二返歌うたりければ、其座にいくらも並居たまへる平家一門の公卿、殿上人、諸大夫、侍に至るまで皆感涙をぞ流されける。入道も面白げにおもひ給ひて「時にとては神妙に申したり。さては舞も見たけれども、今日は紛るゝ事いできたり。此後は召さずとも、常に參て今樣をも歌ひ、舞などを舞て佛なぐさめよ。」とぞ宣ひける。祇王とかくの返事にも及ばず、涙を押へて出でにけり。

annotation.translation: "And so they cried," and since two poems were recited in return, the members of the Taira clan present at that gathering—both high-ranking court nobles and lesser officials, from the highest ministers down to the samurai—all shed tears of emotion. The Retired Emperor, with a delighted expression, thought, "You said it would be a godly matter at that time. Now, having seen the dance, today has become a truly remarkable occurrence. From now on, you need not be summoned; simply come whenever you wish, sing in the current style, and perform dances to console the Buddha," and thus he spoke. Giō could not respond to such words, and suppressing her tears, she withdrew.

text: 「親の命を背かじとつらき道におもむいて、二度、うき目を見つる事の心うさよ。かくて此世にあるならば、又憂き目をも見むずらん。今は只身を投げんとおもふなり。」といへば妹の祇女も「姉身を投げば、われもともに身を投ん。」といふ。母とぢ、是をきくに悲しくていかなるべしともおぼえず。泣々又教訓しけるは「誠に我御前の恨むるもことわりなり。さやうの事あるべしとも知らずして教訓して參らせつる事の心うさよ。但我御前身を[2]投げは、妹もともに身を投げんといふ。二人の娘共に後れなん後、年老衰へたる母命いきてもなにゝかはせむなれば、我もともに身を投げむとおもふなり。いまだ死期も來らぬ親に身を投げさせん事五逆罪にやあらんずらむ。此世は假の宿なり。慚ても慚ても何ならず。唯長き世の闇こそ心うけれ。今生でこそあらめ。後生でだに惡道へ趣かんずる事の悲しさよ。」とさめざめとかき口説ければ、祇王なみだをおさへて「げにもさやうにさぶらはゞ五逆罪疑なし。さらば自害は思ひ止まり候ひぬ。かくて都にあるならば、又うき目をも見むずらん。今は都の外へ出でん。」とて祇王二十一にて尼になり、嵯峨野の奧なる山里に柴の庵をひきむすび念佛してこそ居たりけれ。妹の祇女も「姉身を投げば、我も共に身を投げんとこそ契りしか、まして世を厭はむに誰かは劣るべき。」とて十九にて樣をかへ、姉と一所に籠居て後世を願ふぞあはれなる。母とぢ是をみて若き娘どもだに樣を替る世中に年老い衰へたる母白髮をつけても何にかはせむとて四十五にて髮を剃り、二人の娘諸共に一向專修に念佛して、ひとへに後世をぞ願ひける。

annotation.translation: "I have come upon a hard path, unwilling to turn my back on my parents' lives, and my heart is filled with sorrow for having once seen such sorrowful sights. If I were to remain in this world, I would surely encounter sorrowful sights again. Now I only wish to cast myself away." When she said this, her younger sister Giji also said, "If my sister casts herself away, I too shall cast myself away with her." Her mother, Tochi, upon hearing this, felt such profound grief that she could not think of anything to do. She wept bitterly and admonished them, saying, "Truly, it is only natural that you harbor resentment before me. I never expected such a thing would occur, yet I have admonished you, and my heart is filled with sorrow for this. However, you say that if I cast myself away, you too will cast yourselves away with me. Since the two of you, my daughters, will inevitably be left behind, and even if my aged and declining mother's life were to continue, what could I possibly do? Therefore, I too intend to cast myself away. Would it not be a sin of the Five Heinous Crimes to cause a parent, whose time of death has not yet come, to cast themselves away? This world is but a temporary lodging. No matter how much one feels shame, it is of no avail. Only the long darkness of this life is a cause of sorrow. Surely, it is in this life that one should be. How sad it is to fall even into the evil paths in the next life." As she tearfully pleaded with them, Giko, holding back her tears, said, "Indeed, if one were to act thus, there would be no doubt of committing the Five Heinous Crimes. Then I shall put aside my intention of suicide. If I were to remain in the capital, I would surely encounter sorrowful sights again. Now I shall go out beyond the capital." Thus, at the age of twenty-one, Giko became a nun, dwelling in a brush hut in the remote mountain area of Sagano, practicing nembutsu. Her younger sister Giji also said, "If my sister casts herself away, I too shall cast myself away with her; indeed, I have made this vow. Moreover, who would be more weary of this world than I?" Thus, at the age of nineteen, she changed her appearance and, together with her sister, secluded herself, wishing for the next life—a truly pitiful sight. Their mother, Tochi, upon seeing this, thought, "Even the young girls have changed their appearance in this world; how could I, an aged and declining mother with white hair, do anything?" Thus, at the age of forty-five, she shaved her hair, and the three of them, the two daughters and the mother, devoted themselves entirely to exclusive practice of nembutsu, wishing solely for the next life.

text: かくて春過ぎ夏闌ぬ、秋の初風吹きぬれば、星合の空をながめつゝ、天のと渡る梶の葉に思ふ事かく比なれや。夕日の影の西の山の端に隱るゝを見ても、日の入給ふ所は西方淨土にてあんなり。いつか我等も彼處に生れて物を思はですぐさんずらんと、かゝるにつけても過ぎにし方の憂き事ども思ひ續けて、たゞ盡せぬ物は涙なり。黄昏時も過ぎぬれば竹の編戸を閉じ塞ぎ、燈かすかにかきたてて、親子三人念佛して居たる處に、竹の編戸を、ほと／＼と打ちたゝく者出できたり。その時尼ども膽をけし「あはれ、是はいひかひなき我等が念佛してゐたるを妨げんとて、魔縁のきたるにてぞあるらん。晝だにも人の問ひ來ぬ山里の柴の庵の内なれば、夜深て誰かは尋ぬべき。僅の竹の編戸なれば、あけずとも推破んこと安かるべし。なか／＼たゞあけていれんと思ふなり。それに情をかけずして、命を失ふものならば、年比頼たてまつる彌陀の本願を強く信じて、ひまなく名號を唱へ奉るべし。聲を尋ねて迎へ給ふなる聖衆の來迎にてましませば、などか引接なかるべき。相構へて念佛怠り給ふな。」と、互に心をいましめて、竹の編戸をあけたれば、魔縁にてはなかりけり、佛御前ぞ出できたる。祇王「あれはいかに。佛御前と見奉るは夢かや、うつゝか。」といひければ、佛御前涙をおさへて、「か樣の事申せば、事あたらしう候へども、申さずば、又思ひ知らぬ身ともなりぬべければ、始よりして申すなり。もとよりわらは推參の者にて、出され參らせ候ひしを、祇王御前の申状によてこそ、召し返されても候ふに、女のかひなきこと、我身を心に任せずして、おしとゞめられまゐらせし事心うゝさぶらひしが、いつぞや又めされまゐらせていまやううたひ給ひしにも思しられてこそさぶらへ。いつか我身の上ならんと思へば、嬉しとは更におもはず。障子にまた、『いづれか秋にあはではつべき。』と書置給ひし筆の跡、げにもと思ひさぶらひしぞや。その後は在所をいづくとも知りまゐらせざりつるに、かやうにさまを替て、一處にと承はて後は、あまりに羨しくて常は暇を申しかども、入道殿さらに御用ゐましまさず。つく％＼物を案ずるに、娑婆の榮花は夢の夢、樂み榮えて何かせん。人身は受け難く、佛教には遇ひ難し。此度泥梨に沈みては、多生昿劫をば隔つとも、浮み上らんこと難し。年の若きを憑むべきにあらず。老少不定のさかひ、出づる息の入るをも待つべからず。かげろふ稻妻よりも猶はかなし。一旦の樂に誇りて、後生を知らざらんことの悲しさに、今朝まぎれ出でゝ、かくなりてこそ參りたれ。」とて、かつぎたる衣を打ちのけたるを見れば、尼になてぞ出できたる。「かやうに樣をかへて參りたれば、日比の科をば許し給へ。許さんと仰せられば、諸共に念佛して、一蓮の身とならん。それに猶心行かずば、是よりいづちへも迷ひ行き、如何ならん苔の席、松が根にも倒れ臥し、命のあらんかぎり念佛して、往生の素懷を遂げんとおもふなり。」とさめざめとかきくどきければ、祇王涙をおさへて、「誠にわごぜの是ほどに思ひ給ひけるとは。夢にだに知らず、憂き世の中のさがなれば、身の憂とこそおもふべきに、ともすれば、わごぜの事のみうらめしくて往生の素懷を遂ん事かなふべしともおぼえず、今生も後生も、なまじひに仕損じたるこゝちにてありつるに、かやうにさまをかへておはしたれば、日比の咎は露塵ほども殘らず、今は往生疑ひなし。此度素懷を遂げんこそ何よりも又嬉しけれ。我等が尼になりしをこそ世にためしなきことのやうに、人もいひ我身にも又思ひしか。それは世を恨み身を恨みて成しかば、樣を替るも理なり。今わこぜの出家にくらぶれば事の數にもあらざりけり。わごぜは恨もなし歎もなし。今年は纔に十七にこそなる人の、かやうに穢土を厭ひ、淨土を願はんと、深く思ひいれ給ふこそ、まことの大道心とはおぼえたれ。嬉しかりける善知識かな。いざ諸共に願はん。」とて、四人一所に籠り居て、朝夕佛前に花香を供へ、餘念なく願ひければ、遲速こそありけれ、四人の尼共皆往生の素懷を遂けるとぞ聞えし。されば、後白河の法皇の、長講堂の過去帳にも、祇王、祇女、佛、とぢ等が尊靈と四人一所に入れられけり。あはれなりし事どもなり。

annotation.translation: Thus, when spring passed and summer waned, and the early autumn wind began to blow, gazing at the starry sky of the Star Meeting, could one's thoughts be compared to the leaf of the boat that crosses the heavenly river? Even when seeing the shadow of the setting sun hide behind the western mountain's edge, one knows that the place where the sun sets is the Western Pure Land. "When might we also be born there and think of things, and quickly cross over to the Three Realms?" Even as such things occurred, we continued to think of past sorrowful matters, and the only thing that could not be ended was tears. When the twilight hour had passed, we closed and blocked the bamboo-woven door, barely kindled a lamp, and while the three of us, mother and child, were sitting and chanting the Nembutsu, someone came and began to beat the bamboo-woven door with a sound of 'hotohoto.' At that time, the nuns were frightened and said, "Alas, surely this is a demon coming to disturb our chanting. Even by day, no one comes to ask in this brush hut in the mountain village; at night, who would come to search? Since it is only a bamboo-woven door, it would be easy to push it open without opening it. Yet, we cannot help but want to open it and let them in. If one were to lose one's life without feeling affection, one should strongly believe in the Primal Vow of Amida, which we have relied upon since old times, and chant the Name without cease. Since the Holy Beings come to welcome us, calling out to us, why should they not be received? Do not be negligent in chanting the Nembutsu while facing them." Exchanging these words to encourage one another, they opened the bamboo-woven door, and it was not a demon; it was the Buddha appearing before them. Giō asked, "What is this? Is seeing the Buddha before us a dream or reality?" The Buddha, holding back tears, replied, "If I say such things, it may seem strange, but if I do not speak, I might become someone who has not been made aware of these things again, so I will speak from the beginning. Originally, I was a woman who had been expelled, but by your letter, Lady Giō, I was summoned back. However, I felt sorrow that you, a woman of no worth, did not let your mind rest and instead kept me. When you summoned me again and sang so beautifully, I believed that was the reason I was here. When I thought that I might become like you someday, I felt no joy at all. The traces of the brushwork you had written on the sliding door, 'Which autumn shall we meet and part in?'—I indeed thought of that. After that, I did not know where you were, but after you changed your manner and accepted me to be in one place, I was so envious that I constantly asked for time, yet Lord Nijo never had any further business. Reflecting on all things, the glory and flowers of this world are dreams within dreams; what joy can come from prosperity? It is hard to receive a human body, and hard to encounter the Buddha's teaching. If I sink into Niraya this time, even after many lives and kalpas, it will be difficult to rise again. One should not rely on youth. The boundary of old and young is uncertain; one must not wait for the breath to come in. It is more fleeting than a mayfly or a lightning flash. In the sorrow of not knowing the future life while boasting of a momentary joy, I slipped out this morning and came to be thus." When we saw that she had cast off the clothes she had carried, she appeared as a nun. "Since I have changed my manner thus, please forgive me for my past errors. If you say you will not forgive, we will all chant the Nembutsu together and become one lot. If still your hearts do not move, from now on, I will wander wherever I choose; I will fall and lie down at even a mossy seat or a pine root, and as long as I have life, I will chant the Nembutsu and fulfill my aspiration for rebirth." Crying bitterly and urging them, Giō held back her tears and said, "Truly, you think so deeply of this. I did not even know in a dream, and in this sorrowful world, I should think of my own sorrow, yet often I only resented you and did not think that your aspiration for rebirth could be fulfilled. In this life and the next, I felt that I had carelessly failed. But since you have changed your manner and come thus, there remains not even a speck of dust of my past fault; now there is no doubt of rebirth. To fulfill my aspiration this time is more joyful than anything. When we became nuns, it seemed like an unprecedented thing in the world; people spoke of it, and I also thought so. That was because I hated the world and hated myself, so it is natural to change my manner. But compared to your ordination, my case was nothing. You have no resentment, no sigh. This year, a person of only seventeen years, who so deeply contemplates hating this defiled land and wishing for the Pure Land—this is truly the great mind of the Way. What a joyful good friend! Come, let us all vow together." Then, the four of them secluded themselves in one place, offering flowers and fragrance before the Buddha morning and evening, praying without any other thoughts. Though there were differences in speed, it is said that all four nuns fulfilled their aspiration for rebirth. Therefore, the Emperor Go-Shirakawa had Lady Giō, Lady Giō, Buddha, and Tōji included together as their sacred spirits in the genealogy of the Chōkōdō. Truly, these are pitiful matters.

text: 昔より今に至るまで、源平兩氏朝家に召しつかはれて、王化に隨はず、自朝權を輕んずる者には、互に誡を加しかば、代の亂れもなかりしに、保元に爲義きられ、平治に義朝誅せられて後は、末々の源氏ども、或は流され、或は失はれ、今は平家の一類のみ繁昌して、頭をさし出す者なし。如何ならん末の代までも、何事かあらむとぞ見えし。されども鳥羽院、御晏駕の後は、兵革打ち續き、死罪、流刑、闕官、停任、常に行はれて、海内も靜かならず。世間も末落居せず。就中に永暦應保の比よりして、院の近習者をば、内より御誡あり、内の近習者をば、院より誡めらるゝ間、上下おそれをのゝいて、安い心もなし。只深淵にのぞんで薄氷をふむに同じ、主上上皇、父子の御間には何事の御隔かあるべきなれども、思の外の事どもありけり。是も世澆季に及んで、人梟惡を先とする故なり。主上院の仰を常に申かへさせおはしましける中にも、人耳目を驚し、世以て大きに傾け申すことありけり。

annotation.translation: From ancient times until now, since those who, having been summoned to the imperial court by the Minamoto and Taira clans, did not follow the imperial way and despised the authority of their own court, had been mutually admonished, so that there had been no disturbance of the age, after Tayori was killed in the Hōgen Rebellion and Yoriyoshi was executed in the Heiji Rebellion, the later generations of the Minamoto were either exiled or destroyed, and now only the Taira clan flourishes, with no one daring to raise their head. It seemed that even in the distant future, some matter would arise. However, after the passing of Emperor Toba, warfare continued incessantly; death penalties, exile, vacancies, and suspension of appointments were constantly carried out, and the realm was not peaceful. The world did not remain in decline. Especially from the time of the Eikyō and Ōhō eras onward, since the emperor's close attendants were admonished from within the palace and the palace's close attendants were admonished by the emperor, superiors and inferiors feared one another, and there was no peaceful heart. It was as if one were peering into a deep abyss and treading on thin ice. Although there might be some separation between the reigning emperor and the retired emperor, father and son, extraordinary events occurred. This is because, as the world has declined to its final stages, people have made evil their priority. Even while the emperor and the retired emperor constantly conveyed their instructions to one another, there were matters that astonished the people's eyes and ears and greatly shook the world.

text: 故近衞院の后、太皇太后宮と申しは大炊御門右大臣公能公の御娘なり。先帝に後れ奉らせ給ひて後は、九重の外、近衞川原の御所にぞ移り住ませ給ひける。前の后の宮にて、幽なる御在樣にて渡らせ給ひしが、永歴のころほひは、御年二十二三にもやならせたまひけん、御盛りも少し過させおはしますほどなり。されども、天下第一の美人の聞えまし／＼ければ、主上色にのみ染める御心にて、竊に高力士に詔して、外宮に引き求めしむるに及んで、この大宮へ御艶書あり。大宮敢て聞食しもいれず。されば、ひたすらはやほに現はれて、后御入内あるべきよし、右大臣家に宣旨を下さる。此事天下に於て、異なる勝事なれば、公卿僉議あり、各意見をいふ。「先づ異朝の先蹤をとぶらふに、震旦の則天皇后は、唐の太宗の后、高宗皇帝の繼母なり。太宗崩御の後、高宗の后に立ち給へることあり。それは異朝の先規たる上、別段の事なり。然れども我朝には、神武天皇より以降、人皇七十餘代に及まで、いまだ二代の后に立たせ給へる例を聞かず。」と、諸卿一同に申されけり。上皇も然るべからざるよし、こしらへ申させ給へば、主上仰なりけるは、「天子に父母なし、我十善の戒功によて、萬乘の寶位をたもつ、是程のこと、などか叡慮に任せざるべき。」とて、やがて御入内の日、宣下せられける上は、力及ばせ給はず。

annotation.translation: The former consort of the Konoe-in, who was called Taiho-den no Miya, was the daughter of the Dajō Daijin Kōno no Kimi. After the former Emperor passed away, she moved to reside in the residence at the Kōe no Kawa-hara, outside the Nine Levels. At the previous consort's palace, she lived in seclusion and passed away; however, around the time of the Eiryaku era, she may have been twenty-two or twenty-three years old, and she was in the prime of her life. Nevertheless, having gained a reputation as the most beautiful woman in the land, her heart was devoted solely to the reigning Emperor, and she secretly instructed Takashi no Kishi to have her transferred to the Outer Palace. When this reached the Dajō, the Dajō dared not even hear of it. Therefore, she appeared immediately and openly, and an Imperial Edict was issued to the Dajō's house declaring that she should enter the palace. Since this matter was an unprecedented event in the world, the court nobles held a collective deliberation, each expressing their opinions. 'First, let us look to precedents from foreign courts. In China, the Empress Zetian was the consort of Emperor Taizong of the Tang and the stepmother of Emperor Gaozong. After Taizong's death, she became the consort of Gaozong. That is an exceptional case, as it is a precedent from a foreign court. However, in our own country, from Emperor Jimmu down to the seventy-something emperors, there is no known example of anyone becoming the consort of two successive emperors.' Thus, the court nobles all spoke. The Retired Emperor also ordered that this was improper. When the reigning Emperor declared, 'The Emperor has no parents; I hold the treasure throne of the ten thousand chariots by virtue of the merit of the Ten Precepts. How can such a matter be left to the Imperial consideration?' and the day of her entrance into the palace was proclaimed, no one could oppose it.

text: 大宮かくと聞しめされけるより、御涙に沈ませおはします。先帝に後させ參らせにし久壽の秋のはじめ、同じ野原の露と消え、家をも出、世をも遁れたりせば、かゝる憂き耳をば聞かざらましとぞ、御歎ありける。父の大臣、こしらへ申させ給ひけるは、「世に從はざるを以て、狂人とすと見えたり。既に詔命を下さる。仔細を申すにところなし。只速に參らせ給ふべきなり。もし皇子御誕生ありて、君も國母といはれ、愚老も外祖と仰がるべき瑞相にてもや候ふらむ。是偏に愚老をたすけさせおはします御孝行の御至なるべし。」と、申させ給へども、御返事もなかりけり。大宮その比、なにとなき御手習の次に、

At the beginning of the autumn of Kyūju, when the former Emperor had been made to retire, had she vanished like the dew of the same field, had she left her home and fled the world, she would have wished not to hear such sorrowful news, and she sighed. text: 世にはいかにして漏れけるやらん、哀にやさしきためしにぞ人々申しあへりける。

annotation.translation: I wonder how it has been kept secret in the world; people have spoken of it as a rare and touching incident.
annotation.summary: I wonder how it has been kept secret in the world; people have spoken of it as a rare and touching incident.

text: 既に御入内の日になりしかば、父の大臣供奉の上達部、出車の儀式など、心ことにだしたて參らせ給ひけり。大宮ものうき御出立なれば、とみにもたてまつらず。遙に夜も深け、小夜も半になて後、御車に抜け乘せられ給ひけり。御入内の後は、麗景殿にぞまし／＼ける。ひたすら、朝政をすゝめ申させ給ふ御在樣なり。彼紫宸殿の皇居には、賢聖の障子を立てられたり。伊尹、第伍倫、虞世南、太公望、ろく里先生、李勣、司馬、手長、足長、馬形の障子、鬼の間、李將軍が姿をさながら寫せる障子もあり。尾張守小野道風が、七囘賢聖の障子と書けるも、理とぞ見えし。かの清凉殿の畫圖の御障子には、昔金岡が書きたりし遠山の在明の月もありとかや。故院の未幼主にてましましけるそのかみ、何となき御手まさぐりの次に、かきくもらかさせ給ひしが、ありしながらに少しもたがはぬを御覽じて、先帝の昔もや御戀しくおぼし召されけん。

annotation.translation: Since the day of the imperial entry had already come, the ministers and their retinue, the ministers who attended the father, and the rituals of the carriage, were all prepared with special care. As the departure from the Great Palace was somewhat leisurely, it was not hastened. The night grew deeply late, and after the watch had passed half, she was made to enter the carriage. After the imperial entry, she resided at Reikeiden. She was constantly engaged in the morning administration of state affairs. In that imperial residence of the Shishinden, screens depicting the wise and sage were erected. There were screens portraying Yi Yin, Wu Lun, Yu Shinan, Taigong Wang, the six-lie master, Li Ji, Sima, the long-handed, the long-footed, the horse-shaped, the ghosts' chamber, and the portrait of General Li. Owari-no-kami Ono no Michikaze also wrote the seven wise and sage screens, which appeared to be reasonable. In the paintings of the Seiryoden screens, there were also distant mountains and the moon in the clear sky, as painted by Kanaoka of old. The late Emperor, who had been a young child, while playing with his hands, had written characters that were completely unblemished. Upon seeing this, he may have felt a longing for the former Emperor.

text: さる程に、永萬元年の春の比より、主上御不豫の御事と聞えさせ給ひしが、夏の初になりしかば、事の外に重らせ給ふ。是によて、大藏の大輔伊吉兼盛が娘の腹に、今上の一の宮の二歳にならせ給ふがまし／＼けるを、太子にたてまゐらせ給ふべしと聞えし程に、同六月二十五日、俄に親王の宣旨下されて、やがてその夜受禪ありしかば、天下何となうあわてたるさま也。その時の有職の人々申しあはれけるは、本朝に、童帝の例を尋ぬれば、清和天皇九歳にして、文徳天皇の御禪を受けさせ給ふ。それは彼周公旦の成王に代り、南面にして、一日萬機の政を治め給ひしに准へて、外祖忠仁公、幼主を扶持し給へり。是ぞ攝政のはじめなる。鳥羽院五歳、近衞院三歳にて踐祚あり。かれをこそいつしかなりと申しに、是は二歳にならせ給ふ。先例なし。物さわがしともおろかなり。

annotation.translation: In this manner, from the time of the spring of the first year of Eimon, it was heard that the sovereign was ill, but when early summer came, he became extremely ill. Because of this, when it was heard that the Emperor's first son, who was in the womb of the daughter of the Dazai no Daisuke Yoshinori, was to be made crown prince at the age of two, on the twenty-fifth day of the same month, suddenly an imperial edict was issued to the prince, and that very night there was an abdication; thus the world was in a state of great confusion. The people of the court at that time said: "If we search for precedents of child emperors in our country, Emperor Uda was nine years old when he received the abdication of Emperor Ninmyo. This was modeled after the Duke of Zhou serving as regent for King Cheng, facing south and governing the myriad affairs of state. It was because of this that his maternal grandfather, the Lord Tadami, supported the young sovereign. This was the beginning of the regency. Emperor Toba was five, and Emperor Konoe was three when they ascended the throne. It is said that such a thing has never been done before; this one was made emperor at the age of two. There is no precedent. Even if it is unusual, it is not entirely unreasonable."

text: さる程に、同七月廿七日、上皇竟に崩御なりぬ。御歳二十三。蕾める花の散れるが如し。玉の簾、錦の帳のうち、皆御涙に咽ばせ給ふ。やがて、その夜、香隆寺の艮、蓮臺野の奧、船岡山にをさめ奉る。御葬送の時、延暦寺、興福寺の大衆、額打論といふ事しいだして、互に狼藉に及ぶ。一天の君崩御なて後、御墓所へわたし奉る時の作法は、南北二京の大衆悉く供奉して、御墓所の廻に、わが寺々の額をうつことあり。先づ聖武天皇の御願、爭ふべき寺なければ、東大寺の額をうつ。次に淡海公の御願とて、興福寺の額をうつ。北京には、興福寺に向へて延暦寺の額をうつ。次に天武天皇の御願、教待和尚、智證大師の草創とて、園城寺の額をうつ。然るを山門の大衆、いかがおもひけん、先例を背て、東大寺の次ぎ、興福寺のうへに、延暦寺の額を打つ間、南都の大衆、とやせましかやうせましと僉議するところに、興福寺の西金堂の衆、觀音房、勢至房とて聞えたる大惡僧二人ありけり。觀音房は黒絲威の腹卷に、白柄の長刀くきみじかに取り、勢至房は、萠黄威の腹卷に、黒漆の大太刀もて、二人つと走出で、延暦寺の額をきて落し、散々に打わり、「うれしや水、なるは瀧の水、日はてるとも、絶えずとうたへ。」とはやしつゝ、南都の衆徒の中へぞ入りにける。

annotation.translation: In this manner, on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month, the retired emperor at last passed away. He was twenty-three years of age. Like a flower bud scattering, it was so. Within the jade帘 and the brocade curtains, all were made to choke with tears. Soon that night, he was laid to rest at the northeast corner of Kōryū-ji, at the back of Renzai-dera, at Funadoyama. At the time of the funeral, the great monks of Enryaku-ji and Kōfuku-ji, claiming the matter of 'hitting the forehead,' engaged in mutual violence. After the death of a sovereign, the custom at the time of conveying the remains to the tomb is that the great monks of both the northern and southern capitals all accompany the procession, and there is a practice of striking their temples' tablets around the tomb. First, due to the vow of Emperor Shōmu, there was no temple to contest, so the tablet of Tōdai-ji was struck. Next, as the vow of Prince Ōmi, the tablet of Kōfuku-ji was struck. In the northern capital, the tablet of Enryaku-ji was struck facing Kōfuku-ji. Next, as the vow of Emperor Tenmu, by Master Kyōtai and Great Master Chishō, the tablet of Onjō-ji was struck. However, the great monks of Sanmon, perhaps thinking thus, disregarding precedent, while striking Enryaku-ji's tablet above Kōfuku-ji's, the great monks of the Southern Capital deliberated, saying, 'What should we do? What should we do?' At that time, among the monks of Kōfuku-ji's West Golden Hall, there were two great evil monks known as Kannon-bō and Jizō-bō. Kannon-bō wore a black silk-laced chest plate and held a long sword with a white handle closely at hand; Jizō-bō wore a yellow-dyed silk-laced chest plate and held a large black-lacquered great sword. The two rushed out, knocked down Enryaku-ji's tablet, beat it to pieces, and chanted, 'Happy is the water! It is the water of a waterfall; though the sun sets, it never ceases to flow,' while leading the chant, they entered among the Southern Capital's monks and laypeople.

text: 山門の大衆、狼藉をいたさば、手向へすべき處に、心深うねらふ方もやありけん。一詞も出さず。御門かくれさせ給ひては、心なき草木までも、愁へたる色にてこそあるべきに、この騒動のあさましさに、高きも賤きも、肝魂を失て四方へ皆退散す。同二十九日の午の刻ばかり、山門の大衆おびたゞしう下洛すと聞えしかば、武士、檢非違使、西坂本に馳向て、防ぎけれども、事ともせずおしやぶて亂入す。何者の申出したりけるやらむ、一院、山門の大衆に仰せて、平家を追討せらるべしと聞えし程に、軍兵内裏に參じて、四方の陣頭を警固す。平氏の一類、皆六波羅へ馳集る。一院も、急ぎ六波羅へ御幸なる。清盛公其比、いまだ大納言にておはしけるが、大に恐れさわがれけり。小松殿「何によてか、唯今さる事あるべき。」と、しづめられけれども、上下ののしりさわぐことおびたゞし。山門の大衆、六波羅へは寄せずして、すずろなる清水寺におしよせて、佛閣僧房一宇も殘さず燒はらふ。是はさんぬる御葬送の夜の會稽の耻を雪めんがためとぞ聞えし。清水寺は、興福寺の末寺たるによてなり。清水寺燒けたりける朝、何者の態にや在けん、「觀音火坑變成池はいかに」と札に書て、大門の前にたてたりければ、次の日、又「歴劫不思議力不及」と、返しの札をぞ打たりける。

annotation.translation: The multitude of the Mountain Gate, if they were to commit wanton acts, there might have been some who, in the place where they should have offered themselves up, deeply desired it. They spoke not a single word. When the Imperial Gate was made to hide itself, even the heartless trees and grasses ought to have worn a sorrowful expression, but at the shock of this disturbance, both high and low lost their souls and all retreated in every direction. Around noon on the same twenty-ninth day, it was heard that the multitude of the Mountain Gate had descended into the Lower Capital in great numbers. The warriors and the Kebiishi galloped toward Nishizaka-no-moto to intercept them, yet they pushed through without resistance and burst in. Who it was that made a proposal is unknown; when it was heard that the First Emperor had ordered the multitude of the Mountain Gate to pursue and exterminate the Taira, the troops proceeded to the Imperial Palace and guarded the front lines in all directions. All the kin of the Taira clan rushed to Rokuhara. The First Emperor also hurried to Rokuhara. At that time, Kiyomori was still serving as Dainagon, and he was greatly frightened and agitated. Lady Komatsu said, 'Why should such a thing happen at this very moment?' and tried to calm them, but the upper and lower classes shouted and clamored excessively. The multitude of the Mountain Gate, without stopping at Rokuhara, surged into the somewhat disorderly Kiyomizu Temple, and not leaving a single Buddhist hall or monk's quarters, they set them all ablaze. It was heard that this was to avenge the shame of the funeral ceremony at Kaei, which had been omitted. Kiyomizu Temple was a branch temple of the Kofuku-ji Temple. On the morning when Kiyomizu Temple burned, whoever it was and in whatever state, a plaque reading 'The Avalokiteshvara's fire pit becomes a pool, how is it?' was written and set up before the main gate. The next day, another plaque with the reply 'The miraculous power of countless kalpas is insufficient' was struck in response.

text: 衆徒返り上りければ、一院六波羅より還御なる。重盛卿ばかりぞ、御ともには參られける。父の卿は參られず。猶用心のためかとぞ聞えし。重盛卿、御送よりかへられたりければ、父の大納言の給ひけるは、「一院の御幸こそ大きに恐れおぼゆれ。かねても思しめしより、仰せらるゝ旨のあればこそかうは聞ゆらめ、それにも打解給ふまじ。」とのたまへば、重盛卿申されけるは、「此事ゆめ／＼御けしきにも、御詞にも出させ給ふべからず、人に心附けがほに、中々惡しき御事なり。それにつけても叡慮に背き給はで、人のために御なさけを施させましまさば、神明三寶加護あるべし。さらんにとては、御身の恐れ候ふまじ。」とて、立たれければ「重盛卿は、ゆゝしく大樣なるものかな。」とぞ父の卿ものたまひける。

annotation.translation: When the commoners had turned back and ascended, the Retired Emperor returned from the Sixth of the Sixth Ward. Only Prince Shigemori accompanied him on his journey. His father, the Minister, did not accompany him. It was heard that this was for the sake of caution. Since Prince Shigemori had returned from the escort, his father, the Minister of the Left, said, "The Retired Emperor's journey is truly cause for great fear. Even before you were told, you would have been warned of the matter; that is why it is heard that you have understood. You should not dismiss it lightly." Prince Shigemori replied, "This matter must never be revealed in the slightest in your countenance or in your words. If one were to heed others' thoughts, it would be a very evil thing. Therefore, do not go against your wise judgment; if you were to show compassion for the sake of others, the Three Jewels and the gods would surely protect you. Do not fear for your own safety on that account." Since Prince Shigemori stood up, his father, the Minister, said, "Prince Shigemori is indeed a very great person."

text: 一院還御の後、御前にうとからぬ近習者達あまた候はれけるに、「さても不思議の事を申し出したるものかな。露もおぼし召よらぬものを。」と仰ければ、院中の切者に西光法師といふ者あり。境節御前近う候ひけるが、「天に口なし、人を以ていはせよと申す。平家以外に過分に候間、天の御計らひにや。」とぞ申しける。人々「この事よしなし。壁に耳あり、おそろしおそろし。」とぞ申あはれける。

annotation.translation: After the Emperor returned to his palace, there were many close attendants who were not disliked by the Emperor. He said, 'What a strange thing to have come up. Not even a dewdrop was noticed.' Then, among the high-ranking attendants of the palace, there was a man named Hoshiro Boshi, who was a frequent attendant in the Emperor's presence. He said, 'Heaven has no mouth; let man speak. Since the Taira family has gone beyond what is proper, perhaps this is Heaven's design.' The people then said, 'This matter is ill-omened. There are ears in the walls; it is fearful, fearful.'

text: さる程に、その年は諒闇なりければ、御禊大甞會も行はれず。同十二月二十四日、建春門院その比はいまだ東の御方と申しける御腹に、一院の宮まし／＼けるが、親王の宣旨下され給ふ。

annotation.translation: In this manner, since that year was one of mourning, the great purification and the grand banquet were not held. On the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month, the Emperor issued a decree to Prince Tsuchimikado, who was still in the womb of the Empress Dowager Kenshunmon-in, who was then said to be the Eastern Imperial Consort.

text: 明くれば、改元ありて仁安と號す。同年の十月八日、去年親王の宣旨蒙らせ給し皇子、東三條にて春宮に立たせ給ふ。春宮は御伯父六歳、主上は御甥三歳、何れも昭穆に相叶はず。但し寛和二年、一條院七歳にて御即位。三條院十一歳にて東宮に立せ給ふ。先例なきにしもあらず。主上は二歳にて御禪を受けさせ給ひ、纔に五歳と申二月十九日、東宮踐祚ありしかば、位をすべらせ給て、新院とぞ申ける。いまだ御元服もなくして、太上天皇の尊號あり。漢家本朝是やはじめならむ。

annotation.translation: When the year became clear, there was a change of era name, and it was called Nin'an. On the eighth day of the tenth month of that year, the imperial prince to whom His Majesty had granted the edict of the previous year as crown prince was installed as Crown Prince at Higashi-Sanjo. The Crown Prince was His Majesty's nephew, six years old; the reigning emperor was his uncle, three years old; neither was in accordance with the proper order of generations. However, in the second year of Kanwa, the Daijo Tennō (Emperor Emeritus) ascended the throne at the age of seven; the Sanjo-in (Emperor Sanjo) was installed as Crown Prince at the age of eleven. It was not without precedent. The reigning emperor received abdication at the age of two, and on the nineteenth day of the second month, when he was only five years old, the Crown Prince ascended the throne; His Majesty stepped down, and he was called the New Emperor. Even without having undergone the coming-of-age ceremony, he held the title of Daijo Tennō. Was this not a practice of the Chinese empire that was adopted in our own country?

text: 仁安三年三月二十日、新帝大極殿にして御即位あり。此君の位につかせ給ぬるは、いよ／＼平家の榮花とぞ見えし。御母儀建春門院と申すは、平家の一門にてましますうへ、とりわき入道相國の北の方、二位殿の御妹なり。又平大納言時忠卿と申も、女院の御兄なれば、内の御外戚なり。内外につけたる執權の臣とぞ見えし。叙位除目と申すも、偏にこの時忠卿のまゝなり。楊貴妃が幸ひし時、楊國忠が盛えし如し。世のおぼえ、時のきら、めでたかりき。入道相國天下の大小事をのたまひあはせられければ、時の人平關白とぞ申しける。

annotation.translation: On the 20th day of the 3rd month of the 3rd year of Nin'an, the new emperor held his enthronement ceremony in the Great Court Hall. It was seen as the beginning of the Heike clan's rise to glory, for this emperor was made to ascend the throne by the will of the one who granted it. His mother, known as the Kenchun-mon-in, belonged to the Heike clan; she was the sister of the Second Rank lady, the wife of the retired minister Sogo, the Northern Lady. Also, the Minister of the Left of the Great, Tokitada, was the elder brother of the Imperial Lady, making him a maternal relative of the inner court. He was seen as a minister of authority, closely tied to both the inner and outer circles. Even the appointments to ranks and offices followed the pattern set solely by this Minister Tokitada. It was like the time when Yang Guifei enjoyed favor and Yang Guozhong was at the height of his power. The world was at peace, the times were brilliant, and it was a time of great joy. Since the retired minister Sogo was the one who gave orders on all matters of the land, both great and small, the people of the time called him the Great Regent Heike.

text: さる程に、嘉應元年七月十六日、一院御出家あり。御出家の後も、萬機の政をきこめしされし間、院内わく方なし。院中にちかくめしつかはるゝ公卿殿上人、上下の北面に至るまで、官位俸禄、皆身に餘るばかりなり。されども人の心の習なれば、猶飽きたらで、「あはれその人の亡びたらば、その國はあきなむ、その人失せたらば、その官にはなりなん。」など、疎からぬどちは、寄り合ひ寄り合ひさゝやきあへり。法皇も内々仰なりけるは、「昔より代々の朝敵を平ぐるもの多しといへども、いまだ加樣の事なし。貞盛、秀郷が、將門を討ち、頼義が貞任、宗任を亡し、義家が武平、家平を攻めたりしも、勸賞行はれしこと、受領には過ぎざりき。清盛がかく心のまゝにふるまふこそ然るべからね。これも世末になりて、王法の盡きぬる故なり。」と仰なりけれども、次でなければ御いましめもなし。平家も又別して、朝家を恨み奉ることもなかりしほどに、世の亂れそめける根本は、去じ嘉應二年十月十六日に、小松殿の次男新三位中將資盛卿、その時はいまだ越前守とて十三になられけるが、雪ははだれに降たりけり。枯野の景色まことに面白かりければ、わかき侍ども三十騎ばかりめし具して、蓮臺野や、紫野、右近馬場に打出でて、鷹どもあまたすゑさせ、鶉、雲雀をおたて／＼、終日にかり暮し、薄暮に及んで六波羅へこそ歸られけれ。その時の御攝祿は、松殿にてましましけるが、中御門東洞院の御所より御參内ありけり。郁芳門より入御あるべきにて、東洞院を南へ、大炊御門を西へ御出なる。資盛朝臣、大炊御門猪熊にて、殿下の御出に鼻突に參りあふ。御供の人々「何者ぞ、狼藉なり。御出なるに、乘物より下り候へ／＼。」と、云てけれども、餘に誇り勇み、世を世ともせざりける上、めし具したる侍ども、皆二十より内の若物共なり、禮義骨法辨へたる者一人もなし。殿下の御出ともいはず、一切下馬の禮義にも及ばず、驅け破て通らむとする間、暗さはくらし、つや／＼入道の孫とも知らず。又少々は知たれども、空しらずして、資盛朝臣を始として、侍共皆馬より取て引落し、頗る耻辱に及びけり。資盛朝臣、はふ／＼六波羅へおはして、祖父の相國禪門に、此由訴へ申されければ、入道大きに怒て、「縱ひ殿下なりとも、淨海があたりをば憚り給ふべきに、少者に左右なく、耻辱を與へられけるこそ遺恨の次第なれ。かゝる事よりして、人にはあざむかるゝぞ。此事思ひ知らせ奉らでは、えこそあるまじけれ。殿下を恨奉らばや。」とのたまへば、重盛卿申されけるは「是は少しも苦しう候まじ。頼政、光基など申源氏共にあざむかれて候はんには、誠に一門の耻辱でも候ふべし。重盛が子どもとて候はんずるものの、殿下の御出に參りあひて、乘物より下候はぬこそ尾籠に候へ。」とて、その時事にあうたる侍共めしよせ、「自今以後も、汝等よく／＼心得べし、誤て、殿下へ無禮の由を申さばやとこそ思へ。」とて歸られけり。

annotation.translation: In this manner, on the 16th day of the 7th month of the first year of Ka-i, the Emperor retired to become a priest. Even after his retirement, as he continued to hear and rule over all state affairs, there was no disorder within the retired emperor's palace. The high-ranking nobles and courtiers who served closely in the retired emperor's palace, from the highest to the lowest, including the Northern Palace officials, all held official ranks and stipends that far exceeded their needs. However, since it is the nature of human hearts to be insatiable, even so, without being sated, those who were not distant relatives gathered together and whispered among themselves: 'Alas, when that person dies, that country will be seized; when that person is lost, one will become that official.' The Retired Emperor also said in private: 'From ancient times, there have been many who have pacified the imperial enemies of successive generations, yet there has never been such a case as this. Taira no Tadamori and Minamoto no Yoshiie defeated Satake no Tameyori; Minamoto no Yoritomo and his sons killed Taira no Shigemori and his brother; Minamoto no Yoshitsune attacked Taira no Munemori and his brother. Yet in none of these cases were rewards given that exceeded the rank of provincial governor. Taira no Kiyomori behaving as he does is indeed appropriate. This is because the end of the age has come, and the royal law has exhausted its power.' Although he spoke thus, there was no imperial decree issued subsequently. The Taira clan, moreover, did not even harbor resentment toward the imperial court to such an extent that the root of the world's disorder began to emerge. On the 16th day of the 10th month of the second year of Ka-i, Shigemori, the younger son of the Lord of Komatsu, who was then holding the title of Governor of Echizen and was only thirteen years old, fell into snow. The scenery of Kano was truly delightful, so about thirty young retainers accompanied him. They rode out to Rendo, Shino, and the Right Palace Stables, released many hawks, and chased partridges and larks from morning until evening, spending the entire day in hunting. As twilight approached, they returned to Rokuhara. At that time, the Regent was staying at the Matsudono residence, but he had received a summons from the Imperial Palace at Higashimaru-Higashinotoin. He was to enter through the Ikufu Gate, so he went south from Higashimaru-Higashinotoin and west through the Daigaku-mon Gate. As the Regent was passing by the Daigaku-mon Inokuma, Shigemori no Asomi rode up head-on to meet him. The Retainer's attendants shouted, 'Who are you? This is disorder! Disembark from your horse immediately as the Regent passes!' However, Shigemori was excessively proud and bold, disregarding the world, and the young retainers who accompanied him were all under twenty years of age, with not a single person who understood propriety or protocol. He did not even acknowledge the Regent's passage, let alone show the proper courtesy of dismounting. As they attempted to ride through, the darkness was thick, and they did not realize that they were encountering the grandson of a priest. Even if they knew slightly, they did not hesitate, and starting with Shigemori no Asomi, all the retainers were forcibly pulled from their horses, resulting in great humiliation. Shigemori no Asomi, stumbling and falling, returned to Rokuhara and reported this matter to his grandfather, the Priestly Prime Minister. The Priest became greatly angry and said, 'Even if he is a Prince, one should have refrained from encroaching upon Jinkai's vicinity. To have been humiliated by a youth without regard for right or wrong is indeed a grievous matter. Such things lead to people being deceived. If this matter is not brought to the Prince's attention, it cannot be tolerated. I wish I could hate the Prince.' Shigemori no Asomi replied, 'This should not be so troubling. If Yorimitsu and Mitsuoki and other Minamoto clansmen were deceived, it would indeed be a shame to our entire clan. However, as a child of Shigemori, encountering the Prince's carriage and failing to dismount is indeed indecent.' Then, he summoned the retainers who had been involved in this incident and said, 'From now on, you must all understand this well. If you err and commit disrespect toward the Prince, think of the consequences.' Then he returned.
