text: その後、入道相國小松殿には仰られもあはせず、片田舎の侍どものこはらかにて、入道殿の仰より外は、又恐しき事なしと思ふ者ども、難波妹尾を始として、都合六十餘人召し寄せ、「來二十一日、主上御元服の御定めの爲に殿下御出あるべかんなり。いづくにても待かけ奉り、前驅御隨身共が髻きて、資盛が耻雪げ。」とぞのたまひける。殿下、是をば夢にもしろしめさず、主上、明年御元服、御加冠、拜官の御定のために、御直盧に暫く御座あるべきにて、常の御出よりも引き繕はせ給ひ、今度は待賢門より入御あるべきにて、中御門を西へ御出なる。猪熊堀川の邊に、六波羅の兵ども、直冑三百餘騎待ち受け奉り、殿下を中に取りこめ參らせて、前後より一度に、鬨をどとぞつくりける。前驅御隨身共が今日を晴としやうぞいたるを、あそこに追かけ、こゝに追つめ、馬よりとて引落し、散々に陵礫して、一々に髻をきる。隨身十人が中、右の府生武基が髻もきられにけり。その中に、藤藏人大夫隆教が髻をきるとて、「是は汝が髻と思ふべからず、主の髻と思ふべし。」と、言ひ含めてきてけり。其後に御車の内へも、弓の筈つき入れなどして、簾かなぐり落し、御牛の鞦、胸懸切りはなち散々にし散して、悦のときをつくり、六波羅へこそ參りけれ。入道「神妙なり。」とぞのたまひける。御車副には、因幡のさい使、鳥羽の國久丸といふをのこ、下臈なれども、なさけある者にて、泣々御車つかまつて、中御門の御所へ還御なし奉る。束帶の御袖にて、御涙をおさへつゝ、還御の儀式あさましさ、申すもなか／＼おろかなり。大織冠、淡海公の御事は、擧げて申すに及ばず、忠仁公、昭宣公より以降、攝政關白の、かゝる御目にあはせ給ふ事、未だ承り及ばず。是こそ平家の惡行の始なれ。

annotation.translation: After that, among the samurai of the out-of-the-way provinces, who were insolent and did not fear the Cloistered Regent, and who thought that nothing more fearful existed beyond the Cloistered Lord's commands, starting with Nambe Otomoto, sixty-odd men were summoned. They were told, 'On the twenty-first day of the coming month, because of the Emperor's coming of age ceremony and appointment, His Highness must make an appearance. Wait wherever you can; the vanguard and your personal attendants will gather together, and we will cut off their topknots to avenge Morimori's disgrace.' His Highness did not take this as a dream. For the Emperor's coming of age, hair-capping, and official appointment the next year, he would remain for a time at the Imperial Guard's residence, and instead of his usual appearance, he prepared to enter from the Taimon Gate and emerge from the Nakamikado Gate to the west. At the edge of Inokuma Pond, the soldiers of Rokuhara waited with over three hundred fully armored cavalry. They surrounded His Highness in the center, and from the front and rear, they simultaneously raised a mighty war cry. Seizing the opportunity to avenge their disgrace, they pursued them there, cornered them here, drew them from their horses, dragged them down, and mercilessly cut off their topknots one by one. Among the ten attendants, the topknot of Muneoki of the Right District was also cut off. Among them, Fujiwara no Hidehito, the Doctor Takaokina, while cutting off a topknot, said, 'Do not think this is your own topknot; think of it as your lord's topknot,' and urged them on. After that, inside the imperial carriage, they pulled out the bow's quiver and other items, threw down the blinds, and scattered the ox's harness and breastplate in all directions, creating a scene of delight, and proceeded to Rokuhara. The Cloistered Regent said, 'It is divine and miraculous.' In the carriage's deputy was a man named Toribe no Kunimaru, a messenger from Inaba, a young man of low station, yet a compassionate man. He wept bitterly, serving the carriage, and accompanied the Emperor's return to the Nakamikado Palace. Clad in the formal court robe, holding back his tears, the absurdity of the return ceremony was so great that it could not be described. The matter of the Grand Councillor and Prince Ōmi needs no mention; since Prince Tadanao and Prince Shōsen, no one had yet witnessed a Regent or Chancellor of State being treated in such a manner. This was the beginning of the Heike's evil deeds.

text: 小松殿こそ大に噪がれけれ。行向ひたる侍共、皆勘當せらる。「たとひ入道如何なる不思議を下知し給とも、など重盛に夢をば見せざりけるぞ。凡は資盛奇怪なり、旃檀は二葉よりかうばしとこそ見えたれ。已に十二三歳にならむずる者が、今は禮義を存知してこそ振舞ふべきに、かやうに尾籠を現じて、入道の惡名を立つ、不孝のいたり、汝一人にありけり。」とて、暫く伊勢の國に追ひ下さる。さればこの大將をば、君も臣も御感ありけるとぞ聞えし。

annotation.translation: Lord Komatsu is the one who has caused great noise. All the samurai who were going there have been dismissed. 'Even if the priest gives any strange command, why did he not show a dream to Shigemori? In general, Shigemori is strange. The sandalwood is said to be fragrant from its two leaves. One who is already twelve or thirteen years old should conduct himself now with knowledge of propriety and etiquette, but by displaying such an unsightly act, he has established the priest's bad reputation. The ultimate unfiliality lies with you alone.' So saying, he was exiled for a time to the province of Ise. Thus it was heard that both the lord and the vassal felt moved toward this general.

One who is already twelve or thirteen years old should conduct himself now with knowledge of propriety and etiquette, but by displaying such an unsightly act, he has established the priest's bad reputation. The ultimate unfiliality lies with you alone.' So saying, he was exiled for a time to the province of Ise. Thus it was heard that both the lord and the vassal felt moved toward this general.

text: 是によて主上御元服の御定め、その日は延させ給ぬ。同廿五日、院の殿上にてぞ、御元服の定めはありける。攝政殿さても渡らせ給ふべきならねば、同十二月九日、兼宣旨をかうぶり、十四日太政大臣にあがらせ給ふ。やがて同十七日慶申しありしかども、世の中はにが／＼しうぞ見えし。

annotation.translation: By this, the Emperor's coming-of-age ceremony was determined not to be held on that day. On the same twenty-fifth, the ceremony was held at the院's palace. Since the Regent should not have crossed over, on the same December ninth, Kanezane received the imperial edict, and on the fourteenth he was raised to the position of Chancellor of the Realm. Shortly thereafter, on the seventeenth, there was a celebration, yet the world seemed exceedingly bitter.

text: さる程に今歳も暮ぬ。明れば嘉應三年正月五日、主上御元服あり。同十三日朝覲の行幸ありけり。法皇、女院、待ち受け參らせさせ給て、初冠の御粧いかばかりらうたく思しめされけん。入道相國の御娘、女御に參らせ給ひけり。御歳十五歳。法皇御猶子の儀なり。

annotation.translation: In this manner, the year also drew to a close. On the fifth day of the first month of the third year of Kanei, the sovereign underwent the coming-of-age ceremony. On the thirteenth day of the same month, there was a morning audience and imperial progress. The Retired Emperor, the Empress Dowager, waited to receive him with great honor, and surely they thought how splendid the coronation attire must be. The daughter of the Cloistered Prince and the Great Counselor was made a consort. She was fifteen years of age. She was the niece of the Retired Emperor.

text: 其比妙音院の太政のおほいとの、其時は未内大臣の左大將にてましましけるが、大將を辭し申させ給ふことありけり。時に徳大寺の大納言實定卿、その仁に當り給ふ由聞ゆ。又花山院の中納言兼雅卿も所望あり。その外、故中御門の藤中納言家成卿の三男、新大納言成親卿もひらに申されけり。院の御氣色よかりければ、樣樣の祈をぞ始められける。先づ八幡に百人の僧を籠て、眞讀の大般若を七日讀ませられける最中に、甲良の大明神の御前なる橘の木に、男山の方より山鳩三つ飛來て、食ひ合ひてぞ死にける。鳩は八幡大菩薩の第一の仕者なり。宮寺にかゝる不思議なしとて、時の檢校匡清法印奏聞す。神祗官にして御占あり。天下の噪ぎと占申。「但し君の愼みにあらず、臣下のつゝしみ。」とぞ申ける。新大納言是に恐れをも致されず、晝は人目の滋ければ、夜な／＼歩行にて、中御門烏丸の宿所より、賀茂の上の社へ七夜續けて參られけり。七夜に滿ずる夜、宿所に下向して、苦しさに、うちふし、ちと目睡給へる夢に、賀茂の上の社へ參りたると思しくて、御寶殿の御戸推開き、ゆゝしくけだかげなる御聲にて

annotation.translation: At that time, the Great Minister of the Myōon-in Temple was not yet the Left Great General, but he was the Left Great General; however, he decided to resign from the position of Great General. At that time, it was heard that the Minister of the Left, Sanjō no Saishō, was to be the one to accept this. Furthermore, the Middle Minister of the Hanazono-in, Kōga no Kō, also had a wish. Besides, the third son of the late Middle Minister of the Nakamikado, Fujiwara no Iemochi, the new Minister of the Left, Naruhiro, was also mentioned as a candidate. Since the Emperor's demeanor was favorable, various prayers were begun. First, a hundred monks were stationed at Hachiman, and while the Great Prajñā Pāramitā was being read for seven days, three mountain pigeons flew in from the direction of Otosan, fought over food, and died before the shrine of the Great Deity of Karahara. The pigeons are the first attendants of the Great Bodhisattva of Hachiman. Since there was no such mystery in the imperial temple, the inspector Kyōsei Hōin reported it to the court. The Shrine Department conducted an oracle, which predicted: 'There will be a great uproar throughout the land. However, it is not the fault of the ruler, but of the ministers.' The new Minister of the Left, Naruhiro, was not frightened by this. During the day, people were numerous, so at night he walked repeatedly from his residence at Nakamikado Karasuma to the upper shrine of Kamo, continuing for seven nights. On the night when the seven days were completed, he returned to his residence, feeling unwell, lay down, and dozed off. In his dream, he thought he had gone to the upper shrine of Kamo, pushed open the doors of the Imperial Hall, and heard a very clear and lofty voice.

text:
新大納言猶恐れをも致されず、賀茂の上の社に、ある聖を籠て、御寶殿の御後なる杉の洞に壇を立てて、拏吉尼の法を百日行はせられけるほどに、彼の大杉に雷落ち
かゝり、雷火おびただしく燃え上て、宮中已に危く見えけるを、宮人ども多く走り集て、これを打消つ。かの外法行ひける聖を、追出せんとしければ、「我當社に百日參籠の大願あり、今日は七十五日になる。全く出まじ。」とてはたらかず。此の由を社家より内裏へ奏聞しければ「唯法に任せて追出せよ。」と宣旨を下さる。その時神人白杖を以て、彼聖がうなじをしらけ、一條の大路より南へ追ひ出してけり。神は非禮をうけ給はずと申すに、この大納言、非分の大將を祈り申されければにや、かゝる不思議も出で來にけり。

annotation.translation: The new Dainagon was not afraid at all; at the Upper Shrine of Kamo, he secluded a certain holy man and, in the cedar grove behind the Imperial Treasure Hall, set up an altar, and had the nun Nōkichi perform the ritual for one hundred days. While this was happening, lightning struck that great cedar tree, and countless flames rose up, making the palace appear already in peril. Many palace attendants ran together to extinguish it. Since they sought to expel the holy man who was performing this outer ritual, he said, "I have made a vow to seclude myself at this shrine for one hundred days; today is the seventy-fifth day. I shall not leave at all." Thus, he did not move. When the shrine family reported this to the Imperial Palace, an imperial decree was issued: "Just follow the ritual and expel him." At that time, the shrine attendant struck the holy man's neck with a white staff and drove him south along the main road. The god did not feel insulted, they say, but because this Dainagon prayed to the General of the Non-Rights, such a strange occurrence came to pass.

text: 其比の叙位除目と申は、院内の御はからひにもあらず、攝政關白の御成敗にも及ばず、唯一向平家のまゝにてありしかば、徳大寺、花山院もなり給はず、入道相國の嫡男小松殿、右大將にておはしけるが、左に移りて、次男宗盛、中納言におはせしが、數輩の上臈を超越して、右に加はられけるこそ、申すばかりもなかりしか。中にも徳大寺殿は、一の大納言にて華族、英雄、才覺雄長、家嫡にてまし／＼けるが、越えられ給けるこそ遺恨なれ。定めて御出家などやあらむずらむと、人々内々は申あへりしかども、暫く世のならむ樣を見んとて、大納言を辭し申て、籠居とぞ聞えし。

annotation.translation: The appointment of ranks and offices at that time was not the result of the Emperor's own consideration, nor did it reach the level of the Regent or Chancellor's judgment; it was simply as the Taira clan wished. Consequently, even Daidaiji and Hanazono-in were not appointed, and while the eldest son of the Retired Emperor, Konoe no Daimyōjin, had been Right Great Captain, he was transferred to the Left, and the second son, Munemori, who had been Middle Counselor, was promoted to the Right and appointed to that position. This was so far beyond what any number of senior court ladies could have expected that it was hardly to be believed. Among them, Lord Daidaiji, who was a Great Counselor and a nobleman of great virtue, heroism, talent, and distinction as the family heir, was surpassed, which was a cause of deep resentment. People within the palace speculated that he would surely retire from the world, but he decided to observe how affairs would unfold for a while, resigned from the position of Great Counselor, and was reported to be secluding himself.

text: 新大納言成親卿宣ひけるは、「徳大寺、花山院に越えられたらむは、いかゞせん。平家の次男に越えらるゝこそ安からね。是も萬づ思ふさまなるがいたす所也。いかにもして平家を亡し本望を遂げむ。」とのたまひけるこそ怖しけれ。父の卿は中納言までこそ至られしか。その末子にて、位正二位、官大納言にあがり、大國あまた給はて、子息所從朝恩に誇れり。何の不足に、かゝる心つかれけん。是偏に天魔の所爲とぞ見えし。平治にも、越後中將とて、信頼卿に同心の間、既に誅せらるべかりしを、小松殿やう／＼に申て、首をつぎ給へり。然るにその恩を忘れて、外人もなき所に兵具をとゝのへ、軍兵を語らひおき、其營みの外は他事なし。

annotation.translation: The newly appointed Great Counselor Naruhisa no Kyo stated, 'If I am to transfer to the Tokudaiji or Kazonoin, what shall I do? It is not at ease to be transferred as the second son of the Taira clan. This is indeed a matter of deep thought, but I shall do it. I shall surely destroy the Taira clan and fulfill my long-held wish.' Hearing these words, one felt great fear. His father, the nobleman, had only risen to the rank of Middle Counselor. As the youngest son, he attained the position of Junior Counselor, was elevated to the court rank of Second Rank Senior, and received many provinces. He boasted of his children and the imperial favor bestowed upon them. For what lack did such a heart become so troubled? It seemed to be solely the work of the Heavenly Demon. Even in the Hōji period, Echigo no Chujo, in the company of Shinko no Kyo, should have already been executed; however, through the various pleadings of the Lord Komatsu, his head was spared. Yet, forgetting that favor, in a place without any allies, he assembled weapons and gathered soldiers, and there was nothing else in his camp but these preparations.

text: 東山の麓鹿の谷といふ所は、後は三井寺に續いて、ゆゝしき城郭にてぞありける。俊寛僧都の山庄あり。かれに常は寄りあひ／＼、平家滅さむずる謀をぞ囘しける。或時法皇も御幸なる。故少納言入道信西が子息、淨憲法印御供仕る。その夜の酒宴に、此由を淨憲法印に仰あはせられければ、「あなあさましや、人あまた承候ぬ。唯今漏きこえて、天下の大事に及び候ひなんず。」と大に噪ぎ申ければ、新大納言氣色かはりて、さと立たれけるが、御前に候ける瓶子を、狩衣の袖にかけて引きたふされたりけるを、法皇「あれはいかに。」と仰せければ大納言立かへて、「平氏たふれ候ひぬ。」と申されける。法皇ゑつぼに入らせおはしまして、「物ども參て猿樂つかまつれ。」と仰ければ、平判官康頼參りて、「あゝ餘にへいじの多う候に、もて醉て候。」と申す。俊寛僧都「さてそれをいかゞ仕らむずる。」と申されければ、西光法師「頸を取るにはしかじ。」とて、瓶子の首を取てぞ入にける。淨憲法印餘りのあさましさに、つや／＼物も申されず。返す／＼も恐しかりしことどもなり。與力の輩誰々ぞ。近江中將入道蓮淨俗名成正、法勝寺の執行俊寛僧都、山城守基兼、式部大輔雅綱、平判官康頼、宗判官信房、新平判官資行、攝津國源氏多田藏人行綱を始として北面の輩多く與力したりけり。

annotation.translation: The place called Shigetsu Valley at the foot of Higashiyama was later continued to Miidera, and was a famous castle. There was the mountain villa of Shunken Sōzu. They frequently met there and plotted to destroy the Taira clan. On one occasion, the retired Emperor also came. The son of the former Minister of the Left, the monk Shinzei, named Jōken Hōin, served as an attendant. At the wine banquet that night, since this matter was reported to Jōken Hōin, he loudly cried out, 'Oh, how shocking! Many people have not heard. Now it has leaked out and has reached a matter of great importance for the realm.' The new Dainagon's complexion changed; he tried to rise, but the bottle he was attending to in the presence of the Emperor was caught in the sleeve of his hunting robe and pulled down. The Emperor said, 'What is this?' The Dainagon stood up again and said, 'The Taira clan has been overthrown.' The Emperor, entering a small room, said, 'Have the servants come and perform sarugaku.' The Taira judge Kōrai came and said, 'Ah, there are too many Heiji; let us get drunk.' Shunken Sōzu said, 'Well, how shall we deal with that?' The monk Saikō said, 'It is appropriate to take off the head,' and he took off the neck of the bottle and entered. Jōken Hōin, overwhelmed by the extreme shock, could not utter a single word; even to turn around was terrifying. Who were the supporters? Starting with Michinaga of Ōmi, the monk Renjō (secular name Masanari), Shunken Sōzu, the executor of Hōshō-ji, Motochika, the Governor of Yamashiro, Masatane, the Minister of the Board of Ceremonies, Kōrai, the Taira judge Kōrai, the Taira judge Nobufusa, the new Taira judge Sukuyuki, and Sata no Kōgenji Tadayasu of the Taira clan of Settsu Province, many from the Northern Side served as supporters.

text: 此法勝寺の執行と申すは、京極の源大納言雅俊の卿の孫、木寺の法印寛雅には子なりけり。祖父大納言させる弓箭を取る家にはあらねども、あまりに腹あしき人にて、三條坊門京極の宿所の前をば、人をもやすく通さず、つねは中門にたゝずみ、齒をくひしばり、怒てぞおはしける。かゝる人の孫なればにや、この俊寛も僧なれども、心も猛くおごれる人にて、よしなき謀反にも與しけるにこそ。新大納言成親卿は、多田の藏人行綱を呼て、「御邊をば、一方の大將に憑むなり。此事しおほせつるものならば、國をも庄をも所望によるべし。先づ弓袋の料に。」とて、白布五十端送られたり。

annotation.translation: This Shohooji no Shikibu is said to be the grandson of Konoe no Minno Daigongaku Masatoshi, the son of the Ho-in Kanka of Kidera. Although his grandfather, the Daigongaku, was not a family that excelled in archery, he was a man of extremely bad temper. At the residence of Sanjo-bo-mon Konoe, he would not easily let anyone pass before the main gate, always standing at the middle gate, biting his teeth, and going out only in anger. Because he was the grandson of such a man, perhaps Shunkan, though a monk, was also a man of fierce heart and arrogance, and he even participated in an ill-advised rebellion. The new Daigongaku Narachika summoned Tada no Kurando Yukitsuna, saying, "Regarding the border, rely on one general. If this matter is to be carried out, one may expect the nation or the estate, according to one's desire. First, for the materials of the bow case." Thus, fifty bolts of white cloth were sent.

text: 安元三年三月五日、妙音院殿、太政大臣に轉じ給へるかはりに、大納言定房卿を越えて、小松殿、内大臣になり給ふ。大臣の大將めでたかりき。やがて大饗行はる。尊者には、大炊御門左大臣經宗公とぞ聞えし。一のかみこそ先途なれども、父宇治の惡左府の御例憚あり。

annotation.translation: On the fifth day of the third month of the third year of Angen, when Myōon-in-den transferred to the position of Dajō-daijin, Komon-den became Udaishin, surpassing Dainagon Sadafusa-kyō. It was a great joy for the Minister's Captain. Soon a grand banquet was held. It is said that the revered person was Dajiōmon no Sadanō-kō, the Sadaijin. text:
北面は上古にはなかりけり。白河院の御時、始め置かれてより以降、衞府ども數多候けり。爲俊、盛重、童より千手丸、、今犬丸とて、是等は左右なき切者にてぞありける。鳥羽院の御時も、季教、季頼父子、共に朝家に召仕はれ傳奏する折もありなど聞えしかども、皆身の程をばふるまうてこそありしに、此時の北面の輩は、以外に過分にて、公卿殿上人をも物ともせず、禮儀禮節もなし。下北面より上北面にあがり、上北面より殿上の交を許さるゝ者もあり。かくのみ行はるゝ間、おごれる心どもも出きて、よしなき謀反にも與しけるにこそ。中にも故少納言入道信西が許に召使ける師光成景といふものあり。師光は阿波の國の在廰、成景は京の者、熟根賤しき下臈なり。健兒童、もしは恪勤者などにて被召仕けるが、賢々しかりしによりて、師光は左衞門尉、成景は右衞門尉とて、二人一度に靱負尉になりぬ。信西が事にあひし時、二人と
もに出家して、左衞門入道西光、右衞門入道西敬とて、此等は出家の後も、院の御倉預にてぞ在ける。

annotation.translation: In ancient times, there were no Hyōmen; they were first established during the reign of Emperor Shirakawa, and since then, many members of the E-fu have served. Taka-toshi, Morishige, and from childhood, Chijūmaru... now known as Inumaru—these were all fearless swordsmen without left or right. During the reign of Emperor Toba, the father and son duo, Sue-nori and Sue-yori, were summoned to the Imperial Court and sometimes served as Chūsō, as reported; yet all of them behaved according to their station. In contrast, the Hyōmen of this time were excessively arrogant, showing no regard for the Kōkyō or Dajōjin, and lacking all propriety and etiquette. Some rose from the lower Hyōmen to the upper Hyōmen, and from the upper Hyōmen were permitted to associate with the Dajōjin. As this continued, arrogant minds arose, and they even participated in base rebellions. Among them was a man named Shikō, who was summoned and employed at the residence of the late Shōnagon In'ō, Shinzei. Shikō was from the province of Awa; Naritsune was from Kyoto; both were of humble, lowly birth. Though they were summoned as talented youths or diligent servants, due to their cleverness, Shikō became the Left Guard Lieutenant, and Naritsune the Right Guard Lieutenant, and both simultaneously became Yūfu-jo. When Shinzei's affair occurred, both of them took the tonsure, becoming the Left Guard In'ō Seikō and the Right Guard In'ō Seikei, and even after their ordination, they remained in charge of the Emperor's Imperial Granaries.

text: かの西光が子に、師高といふ者あり。是も切者にて、檢非違使五位尉に歴上て、安元元年十二月廿九日、追儺の除目に加賀守にぞなされける。國務を行ふ間、非法非禮を張行し、神社佛寺、權門勢家の庄領を沒倒し、散々の事共にてぞありける。假令せう公が跡を隔つといふとも、穩便の政を行ふべかりしに、かく心のまゝにふるまひし程に、同二年夏の比、國司師高が弟、近藤判官師經、加賀の目代に補せらる。目代下著のはじめ、國府の邊に鵜川といふ山寺あり。寺僧どもが境節湯をわかいて浴びけるを、亂入しておひあげ、我身あび、雜人共おろし、馬洗はせなどしけり。寺僧怒をなして、「昔より此處は國方の者入部することなし。速に先例に任せて、入部の押妨をとゞめよ。」とぞ申ける。「先先の目代は、不覺でこそいやしまれたれ。當目代はその儀あるまじ。唯法に任せよ。」といふ程こそありけれ、寺僧どもは、國方の者を追出せむとす。國方の者共は次を以て、亂入せんとす。うちあひ張合ひしける程に、目代師經が秘藏しける馬の足をぞ打折りける。その後は互に弓箭兵仗をたいして、射合ひ截合ひ數刻戰ふ。目代かなはじとや思ひけむ、夜に入て引退く。其後當國の在廳ども催し集め、其勢一千餘騎鵜川に押寄せて、坊舎一宇も殘さず燒拂ふ。鵜川といふは、白山の末寺なり。この事訴へんとて進む老僧誰々ぞ。智釋、學明、寶臺房、正智、學音、土佐阿闍梨ぞ進みける。白山三社、八院の大衆、悉く起りあひ、都合その勢二千餘人、同七月九日の暮方に、目代師經が館近うこそ押寄せたれ。今日は日暮れぬ。明日の軍と定めて、その日はよせでゆらへたり。露ふき結ぶ秋風は、射向の袖を飜し、雲井を照す稻妻は冑の星を耀す。目代かなはじとや思ひけん、夜逃にして京へのぼる。明くる卯刻に押寄て、閧をどとつくる。城の中には音もせず。人を入れて見せければ、皆落て候と申す。大衆力及ばで引退く。然らば山門へ訴へんとて、白山中宮の神輿をかざり奉り、比叡山へふりあげ奉る。同八月十二日の午刻許、白山の神輿、既に比叡山東坂本につかせ給ふと云程こそありけれ。北國の方より雷おびたゞしく鳴て、都をさして鳴りのぼる。白雪くだりて地を埋み、山上洛中おしなべて、常葉の山の梢まで皆白妙になりけり。

annotation.translation: There was a man named Motosaka among the children of that Sai-ko. He too was a warrior; having advanced to the position of Junior Fifth Rank, Assistant Commander of the Bureau of Police, on the 29th day of the 12th month of the first year of Anji, he was appointed Governor of Kaga. While exercising state power, he committed illegal and unrighteous acts, confiscating the manors of shrines, Buddhist temples, powerful families, and aristocratic houses. He engaged in numerous improper deeds. Even if he were to distance himself from the Imperial lineage, he should have conducted himself with prudence and propriety; yet, as he acted according to his own whims, in the summer of the second year of that reign, the Governor of the province, Motosaka's younger brother, Kondo no Gonojo Motosune, was appointed as the deputy governor of Kaga. At the beginning of the deputy governor's arrival at his post, there was a mountain temple called Ukigawa on the outskirts of the provincial capital. The monks of the temple were dividing the water of the hot spring to bathe in it. He barged in, took the bath for himself, drove away the commoners, and made them wash his horses. The monks of the temple became angry and said, 'Since ancient times, no one from the provincial government has entered this place. Quickly, in accordance with precedent, stop the entry and obstruction.' There was a time when he said, 'The previous deputy governor was reprimanded because he was unaware. This deputy governor must not have such an excuse. Rely solely on the law.' The monks of the temple then sought to drive out the men from the provincial government. The men from the provincial government, in turn, intended to break in. As they clashed and struggled, the deputy governor Motosune's horse, which he had kept in secret, had its leg broken. After that, they faced each other with bows, arrows, weapons, and shields, shooting and cutting at each other, fighting for several hours. Perhaps thinking that the deputy governor could not prevail, he withdrew into the night. After that, the officials of the province gathered, and their force, numbering over a thousand riders, pressed upon Ukigawa, burning down every single temple building without leaving a single one. Ukigawa is a branch temple of Mount Haku. Who was the old monk who advanced to bring this matter to complaint? Chishaku, Gakumei, Houdai-bou, Shouji, Gakuon, and Tosa Ajari advanced. The great assembly of the three shrines and eight monasteries of Mount Haku all rose up, and in total their force numbered over two thousand people. On the evening of the 9th day of the 7th month of that year, they pressed upon the residence of the deputy governor Motosune. Today the sun has set. Deciding to make war tomorrow, that day they held back. The autumn wind, which binds the morning dew, turns the sleeves of those aiming their bows; the lightning shining in the clouds illuminates the star-patterned helmets. Perhaps thinking that the deputy governor could not prevail, he fled by night and ascended to the capital. At the hour of the hare the next day, they pressed upon him, making a great clamor. Inside the castle there was no sound. When they were allowed to enter and see, they were told that everyone had fled. The assembly, unable to exert their strength, withdrew. Then, intending to bring a complaint to the mountain gate, they adorned the portable shrine of the Middle Palace deity of Mount Haku and raised it to Hieizan. By around noon on the 12th day of the 8th month of that year, it was said that the portable shrine of Mount Haku had already reached Higashisakamoto on the eastern slope of Hieizan. From the direction of the northern provinces, thunder roared incessantly, ascending toward the capital. Snow descended, filling the ground. From the mountain top to the capital, everything, even the tops of the evergreen mountains, turned completely white.

text: 神輿をば、客人の宮へ入れ奉る。客人と申は、白山妙理權現にておはします。申せば父子の御中なり。先沙汰の成否は知らず、生前の御悦、只この事にあり。浦島が子の七世の孫に遭へりしにも過ぎ、胎内の者の靈山の父を見しにも超えたり。三千の衆徒踵をつぎ、七社の神人袖を列ね、時々刻々の法施、祈念、言語道斷の事ども也。

annotation.translation: The portable shrine is to be carried into the guest's palace. By 'guest' is meant the White Mountain Myōri Gongen, who resides there. To explain, he is the father and son together. As for the outcome of the previous matter, I do not know, but the joy of his living life is found only in this matter. This surpasses even Urashima's grandson meeting his great-grandson after seven generations, and it exceeds the spirit child seeing his father, the Spirit Mountain, from within the womb. Three thousand disciples follow in succession, and the seven shrine priests stand shoulder to shoulder. The Dharma practice, prayers, and words beyond the path of language, occurring moment by moment, are such things.

text: 山門の大衆、國司加賀の守師高を流罪に處せられ、目代近藤判官師經を禁獄せらるべき由奏聞す。御裁斷遲かりければ、さも可然公卿殿上人は、「あはれとく御裁許あるべきものを、昔より山門の訴訟は他に異なり、大藏卿爲房、太宰の權帥季仲は、さしも朝家の重臣たりしかども、山門の訴訟によて、流罪せられにき。況や師高などは、事の數にやはあるべきに、子細にや及ぶべき。」と申あはれけれども、「大臣は祿を重んじて諫めず、小臣は罪に恐れて申さず。」といふ事なれば、各口を閉ぢたまへり。「賀茂川の水、雙六の賽、山法師、これぞ我心にかなはぬもの。」と白河院も仰なりけるとかや。鳥羽院の御時、越前の平泉寺を、山門へつけられけるには、當山を御歸依淺からざるによて、「非を以て理とす。」とこそ、宣下せられて、院宣をば下されけれ。江帥匡房卿の申されし樣に、「神輿を陣頭へ振奉て、訴申さんには、君はいかゞ御計ひ候ふべき。」と申されければ、「げにも山門の訴訟はもだしがたし。」とぞ仰せける。

annotation.translation: The great multitude of the Mountain Gate had the State Governor of Kaga, Mochitaka, exiled, and reported that the acting governor, Konoto no Gon no Kami Mochitsune, should be imprisoned. Because the Imperial judgment was delayed, the high-ranking court nobles and palace officials said, "Alas, he should have been granted judgment; but since ancient times, the Mountain Gate's lawsuits have been different from others. Even Ōkurashō Muraie and Dazai no Gon no Shōki, who were so heavy ministers of the Imperial House, were exiled due to the Mountain Gate's lawsuits. How much more should Mochitaka and others, in terms of the number of cases, be investigated in detail?" Yet, because "the Minister does not remonstrate, cherishing his salary, and the low-ranking officials do not speak, fearing punishment," they all closed their mouths. "The water of the Kamo River, the dice of sugoroku, the mountain monks—these are things that do not suit my heart." So the Emperor Shirakawa also said. When Emperor Toba reigned, the Eizen-ji of Echizen was attached to the Mountain Gate; because the Mountain was not a slight place of refuge for the Emperor, it was proclaimed, "Wrong is taken as right," and an Imperial edict was issued. As the Minister of the Right, Masafusa, had said, "If we were to carry the portable shrine to the head of the army and present a petition, how would the Emperor plan to deal with it?" Since it was said thus, he replied, "Indeed, the Mountain Gate's lawsuits are indeed difficult to bear."

text: 去じ嘉保二年三月二日、美濃守源義綱朝臣、當國新立の庄を倒す間、山の久住者圓應を殺害す。是によて日吉の社司、延暦寺の寺官、都合三十餘人、申文をささげて陣頭へ參じけるを後二條關白殿、大和源氏中務權少輔頼春に仰せてふせがせらる。頼春が郎等矢を放つ。矢庭に射殺さるゝ者八人、疵を被むる者十餘人、社司諸司四方へちりぬ。山門の上綱等、仔細を奏聞のために下洛すと聞えしかば、武士、檢非違使、西坂本に馳向て、皆おかへす。

annotation.translation: On the second day of the third month of the second year of Kayhō, Minoshu Gen Yoshitsuna no Asomi, while destroying the newly established estates in that province, killed Enō, who had been residing in the mountains for a long time. Because of this, the priests of the Hiyoshi shrine and the temple officials of Enryaku-ji, totaling more than thirty persons, presented a petition to the camp commander. The latter, the Dainagon of the Second Ōjō, was ordered by Dairō no Chūjō no Gon-shōyū Yoriharu of the Yamato Genji to restrain them. Yoriharu's retainers shot arrows; eight persons were shot down in the midst of the arrows, and more than ten were wounded. The shrine priests and other officials scattered in all directions. Hearing that the head monks of the Mountain Gate had come down to the capital to report the details, the warriors and the Keiibi-shi galloped to Nishizakamoto and turned them all back.

text: 山門には、御裁斷遲々の間、七社の神輿を根本中堂に振上げ奉り、その御前にて、眞讀の大般若を七日讀で、關白殿を呪咀し奉る。結願の導師には、仲胤法印、その比はいまだ仲胤供奉と申しが、高座に上り、かね打ならし、表白の詞にいはく、「我等なたねの二葉よりおふし立て給ふ神達、後二條の關白殿に、鏑矢一つ放ち當て給へ、大八王子權現。」と高らかにぞ祈誓したりける。やがてその夜不思議の事あり。八王子の御殿より、鏑矢の聲いでて、王城をさしてなん行くとぞ、人の夢には見たりける。そのあした、關白殿の御所の御格子をあげけるに、只今山よりとてきたるやうに、露にぬれたる樒、一枝たたりけるこそ怖しけれ。やがて山王の御咎めとて、後二條の關白殿、重き御病をうけさせ給ひしかば、母上、大殿の北の政所大に歎かせ給つゝ、御樣をやつし、賤しき下臈のまねをして、日吉の社に御參籠あて、七日七夜が間祈申させ給けり。あらはれての御祈には、百番の芝田樂、百番の一物、競馬、流鏑馬、相撲各百番、百座の仁王講、百座の藥師講、一ちやく手半の藥師百體、等身の藥師一體並に釋迦、阿彌陀の像、各造立供養せられけり。又御心中に、三つの御立願あり。御心のうちの事なれば、人いかで知り奉るべき。それに不思議なりし事は、七日に滿ずる夜、八王子の御社にいくらもありける參人どもの中に、陸奧より遙々と上りたりける童神子、夜半ばかりに俄にたえ入けり。遙にかき出して祈りければ、程なくいき出て、やがて立て舞ひかなづ。人奇特の思をなして是を見る。半時ばかり舞て後、山王おりさせ給て、やう／＼の御託宣こそ恐しけれ。「衆生等確に承れ。大殿の北の政所、今日七日我が御前に籠らせ給たり。御立願三つあり。一つには今度殿下の壽命を助けてたべ、さも候はゞ、下殿に候ふ諸のかたはうどに交て、一千日が間、朝夕宮仕申さんとなり。大殿の北の政所にて、世を世とも思し召さで、すごさせ給ふ御心に、子を思ふ道にまよひぬれば、いぶせきことも忘れて、あさましげなるかたはうどに交はて、一千日が間、朝夕宮仕申さむと仰せらるゝこそ、誠に哀に思しめせ。二つには、大宮の波止土濃より八王子の御社まで、囘廊作て參らせむとなり。三千人の大衆、降にも照にも、社參の時いたはしうおぼゆるに、囘廊作られたらば、いかにめでたからん。三つには今度の殿下の壽命を助させ給はゞ、八王子の御社にて、法花問答講毎日退轉なく行べしとなり。何れもおろかならねども、かみ二つはさなくともありなむ。毎日法花問答講は、誠にあらまほしうこそ思召せ。但今度の訴訟は、むげに安かりぬべき事にてありつるを、御裁許なくして、神人宮仕射殺され、疵を被り、泣く泣く參て訴申す事の餘に心憂て、如何ならむ世までも忘るべしともおほえず。その上かれらに當る處の矢は、しかしながら和光垂跡の御膚に立たるなり。誠か虚言か是を見よ。」とて、肩ぬいだるを見れば、左の脇の下、大なるかはらけの口ばかりうげのいてぞ見えたりける。「是が餘に心憂ければ、如何に申とも、始終のことは叶ふまじ。法花問答講一定あるべくば、三年が命を延べて奉らむ。それを不足に思し召さば、力及ばず。」とて山王あがらせ給ひけり。母上は御立願の事、人にも語らせ給はねば誰漏しつらむと、少しも疑ふ方もましまさず。御心の内の事どもを、ありのまゝに御託宣ありければ、心肝にそうて、ことに貴くおぼしめし、泣々申させ給けるは「縱ひ一日片時にて候ふとも、ありがたうこそ候ふべきに、まして三年が命を延べて給らむ事しかるべう候ふ。」とて、泣々御下向あり。急ぎ都へ入せ給て、殿下の御領紀伊國に、田中庄といふ所を、八王子の御社へ永代寄進せらる。それよりして法花問答講、今の世に至るまで毎日退轉なしとぞ承る。

annotation.translation: While the Imperial Court deliberated at the Gate of the Mountain, the seven divine palanquins were lifted to the Great Central Hall of the Root, and before the Imperial Presence, the Great Perfection of Wisdom was read aloud over seven days, and prayers of cursing were offered to the Chancellor. The chief priest for the completion of the rites was the Dharma Master Naka-tane; at that time he was still called Naka-tane the Attendant. He ascended the high seat, beat the drum, and in the declaration of the confession he said: 'O divine beings, who were born from the two leaves of the seed, we pray that you send one arrow to the Chancellor of the Second Gojo, the Great Eight Princes Gongen.' He prayed aloud with great fervor. That very night, an extraordinary event occurred. From the palace of the Eight Princes, the sound of an arrow was heard, and it seemed to travel toward the capital, as people recounted in their dreams. On the following morning, when the lattice of the Chancellor's palace was raised, a single branch of rosemary, as if it had just come from the mountain, lay wet with dew, and this was truly frightening. As a consequence of the wrath of the Mountain God, the Chancellor of the Second Gojo fell gravely ill. His mother, deeply distressed, had him change into the attire of a humble servant, and for seven days and nights he secluded himself in the Shrine of Hie, offering prayers. In the public prayers, there were performed: one hundred bouts of Shiba-da-gaku, one hundred bouts of Ichimono, horse racing, yabusame, sumo wrestling, each one hundred bouts; one hundred assemblies of the Nio; one hundred assemblies of Yakushi; one hundred and fifty Yakushi statues; life-sized statues of Yakushi, Shaka, and Amida, all of which were crafted and offered as acts of worship. Furthermore, there were three vows made in his heart. Since these were matters of his inner thoughts, how could anyone know them? What was most extraordinary was that on the night when the seven days were completed, among the many visitors to the shrine of the Eight Princes, a young boy deity who had traveled a great distance from Mutsu suddenly fell silent around midnight. When he was vigorously roused and prayed to, he soon revived, stood up, and began to dance. People, thinking this to be a strange occurrence, watched him. After dancing for about half an hour, the Mountain God descended and spoke various divine oracles, which were truly frightening. 'All living beings, listen carefully. The Chancellor of the Second Gojo has secluded himself before my shrine today for seven days. He has made three vows. First, if you save the life of His Highness this time, then, if so, among all the servants of the lower court, he will serve in the palace morning and evening for one thousand days. Because the Chancellor of the Second Gojo, not regarding the world as the world, has allowed his heart to wander into the path of a father's love, forgetting all base matters, he will mingle with those strange servants and serve in the palace morning and evening for one thousand days. This is what he has declared, and truly, you should feel deep compassion. Second, from the harbor of the Great Palace in Tosa to the shrine of the Eight Princes, I will have a covered corridor built. With three thousand great crowds, whether in rain or shine, the visit to the shrine is extremely tiresome; if a covered corridor were built, how wonderful that would be. Third, if you save the life of His Highness this time, at the shrine of the Eight Princes, the Dharma Flower Debate Assembly will be held every day without cessation. Although none of these are trivial, at least the first two could be granted. The daily Dharma Flower Debate Assembly is truly what is desired. However, the lawsuit this time, which should have been settled easily, resulted in the people of the shrine and the court being killed without the Imperial Court's permission, receiving wounds, and tearfully coming to appeal; thus, the heart is so troubled that even the world to come is forgotten. Moreover, the arrow that struck them was, after all, standing upon the skin of the Buddha, who descended to manifest in the world. Whether this is true or false, behold it.' Upon hearing this, they saw that his shoulder was bare, and on the left side of his armpit, a large mouth of a skull was gaping open. 'Because this is so troubling, no matter what I say, the entirety of the matter cannot be accomplished. If the Dharma Flower Debate Assembly is certain to be held, I will extend my life for three years to fulfill it. If you consider this insufficient, I lack the power.' Thus, the Mountain God ascended. Since his mother did not tell anyone of the vows he had made, who could have leaked them? She had no doubt at all. Because the matters of his heart were revealed exactly as they were in the divine oracle, she felt deeply moved, regarded them as particularly noble, and with tears said, 'Even if it were only for one day or a moment, it would indeed be most grateful; how much more so to extend his life for three years, which is truly fitting.' With tears, she descended. Hastening to enter the capital, in the Chancellor's domain of Kii Province, a place called Tanaka Estate, she permanently donated it to the shrine of the Eight Princes. From that time on, the Dharma Flower Debate Assembly has been held every day without cessation up to the present age, as we have heard.'

text: かゝりし程に、後二條關白殿、御病かろませ給て、もとの如くにならせ給ふ。上下喜びあはれし程に、三年の過ぐるは夢なれや、永長二年になりにけり。六月二十一日、又後二條の關白殿、御髮の際に惡しき御瘡出きさせ給て、打ち臥させ給ひしが、同二十七日、御年三十八にて終にかくれさせ給ぬ。御心の猛さ、理の強さ、さしもゆゝしき人にてましましけれ共、まめやかに事の急になりしかば、御命を惜ませ給ひける也。誠に惜しかるべし。四十にだにも滿たせ給はで、大殿に先立まゐらせ給こそ悲しけれ。必ずしも父を先立つべしといふことはなけれども、生死のおきてに順ふならひ、萬徳圓滿の世尊、十地究竟の大士達も、力及び給はぬ事どもなり、慈悲具足の山王、利物の方便にてましませば、御咎めなかるべしとも覺えず。

annotation.translation: As it was thus, after the Dajō Daijin of the Second Jōjo, the illness became lighter and he was restored to his former state. While the people above and below rejoiced and felt compassion, three years had passed like a dream, and it had become the second year of Eishō. On the twenty-first day of the sixth month, again the Dajō Daijin of the Second Jōjo was afflicted with a terrible sore at the nape of his neck; he was made to lie down, but on the twenty-seventh day, at the age of thirty-eight, he passed away. Though he was a person of such great spirit and strong reason, since matters suddenly turned critical, he could not save his life. Truly, it is a thing to be regretted. He was not allowed to reach even forty years of age, and it is sorrowful that he departed before the Great Minister. It is not that one must necessarily die before one's father; it is simply the natural order of life and death. Even the World Honored One, who has perfected all virtues, and the great Bodhisattvas who have attained the tenth stage, cannot exert power to change this. Since the Mountain King, endowed with compassion, acts for the benefit of others through expedient means, one cannot feel that he would be at fault.

text: さる程に山門の大衆、國司加賀守師高を流罪に處せられ、目代近藤判官師經を禁獄せらるべき由、奏聞度々に及ぶといへども、御裁許なかりければ、日吉の祭禮を打ち留めて、安元三年四月十三日辰の一點に、十禪師、客人、八王子三社の神輿かざり奉りて、陣頭へ振奉る。下松、きれ堤、賀茂の川原、糺、梅たゞ、柳原、東北院の邊に、しら大衆、神人、宮仕、専當みち／＼て、幾らといふ數を知らず、神輿は一條を西へいらせ給ふ。御神寶天にかゞやいて、日月地に落給かと驚かる。是によて、源平兩家の大將軍、四方の陣頭を固めて、大衆防ぐべきよし仰下さる。平家には、小松の内大臣の左大將重盛公、其勢三千餘騎にて、大宮面の陽明、待賢、郁芳、三つの門をかため給ふ。弟宗盛、知盛、重衡、伯父頼盛、教盛、經盛などは、西南の陣を固められけり。源氏には、大内守護の源三位頼政卿、渡邊の省授をむねとして、その勢僅に三百餘騎、北の門、縫殿の陣を固め給ふ。處は廣し、勢は少し、まばらにこそ見えたりけれ。

annotation.translation: In due course, the great multitude of the Sanmon was ordered to exile the Kokushi Kagano no Kami Shitaka, and despite repeated petitions to have the substitute Konno no Gon no Kami Shike imprisoned, since the Imperial permission was not granted, they halted the Hie festival and, on the 13th day of the 4th month of the third year of Gen'gen, at the hour of the Dragon, adorned the palanquins of the Ten Zen Masters, the Guest, and the three shrines of the Hachioji, and carried them in procession to the headquarters. At Shimomatsu, Kire-zaka, the banks of the Kamo River, Tadasu, Ume-tada, Yanagihara, and the vicinity of the Tōhoku-in, the great multitude, the shrine attendants, the palace servants, and the dedicated officials, one after another, were so numerous that their number could not be counted. The palanquins were commanded to proceed westward along a single line. The sacred treasures shone in the heavens, as if the sun and moon had fallen to earth, causing amazement. On this account, the great generals of the Minamoto and Taira clans were ordered to secure the headquarters in all four directions and to defend the multitude. In the Taira camp, the Minister of the Left Shigemori, son of the Small Pine, with his force of over three thousand cavalry, fortified the Yang Gate, the Machiken Gate, and the Ikuyō Gate, the three gates facing the Great Palace. His younger brother Tokimori, Tomomori, Shigemori, his uncle Yorimori, Norimori, and Kanemori, among others, fortified the southwestern headquarters. In the Minamoto camp, the Lord of the Great Inner Guard, the Vice-Minister Yoshimasa of the Third Rank, taking the province of Watanabe as his base, with his force of barely over three hundred cavalry, fortified the northern gate and the Naidō headquarters. The place was vast, the force was small, and it appeared somewhat sparse.

text: 大衆無勢たるによて、北の門、縫殿の陣より、神輿を入れ奉らんとす。頼政卿さる人にて、馬よりおり冑をぬいで、神輿を拜し奉る。兵ども皆かくの如し。衆徒の中へ使者を立てゝ、申送る旨あり。その使は、渡邊の長七唱と云者なり。唱その日は、きちんの直垂に、小櫻を黄にかへいたる鎧著て、赤銅作の太刀を帶き、白羽の箭負ひ、滋籐の弓脇にはさみ、冑をばぬぎ高紐に掛け、神輿の御前に畏て申けるは、「衆徒の御中へ源三位殿の申せと候。今度山門の御訴訟、理運の條勿論に候。御成敗遲々こそよそにても遺恨に覺え候へ。さては神輿入れ奉らむこと仔細に及び候はず。但頼政無勢に候ふ。その上明けて入れ奉る陣より入せ給て候はば、山門の大衆は目たりがほしけりなど、京童の申候はむこと、後日の難にや候はんずらむ。神輿を入れ奉らば、宣旨を背くに似たり。又防ぎ奉らば年來醫王、山王に首を傾け奉て候ふ身が、今日より後、弓箭の道に分れ候ひなむず。彼と云ひ、此といひ、旁難治のやうに候。東の陣は、小松殿大勢で固められて候。其陣より入らせ給ふべうもや候ふらむ。」と、いひ送たりければ、唱がかくいふに防がれて、神人、宮仕暫くゆらへたり。

annotation.translation: Since the common people were powerless, they intended to carry the mikoshi from the Northern Gate and the Nōdono camp. Yorimasa, who was a certain man, dismounted from his horse, removed his armor, and offered a bow to the mikoshi. All the soldiers did likewise. A messenger was sent into the ranks with a message to be delivered. That messenger was a man named Watanabe no Nagashichi Shō. On that day, Shō wore a properly made hitatare, a suit of armor dyed with small cherry blossoms in yellow, carried a copper-colored tachi, bore white-feathered arrows, and had a Shitō bow tucked at his side; he took off his helmet and hung it on a high cord. Reverently, he said before the mikoshi: 'From Lady Gen Sanmi, a message to the ranks: This time, regarding the temple's grievance, the matter of fate is beyond question. If your judgment is delayed, it will surely be remembered as a lingering resentment by outsiders. Therefore, there is no need to consider carrying the mikoshi. However, Yorimasa is powerless. Moreover, if they were to enter from the camp at dawn, the common people of the temple might say something like, "The common people of Kyoto will be looking on," which would become a difficulty in the future. If we carry the mikoshi, it would resemble betraying the imperial edict. If we try to defend, I, who have bowed my head to Iwai and Sanō for many years, will, from today onward, be divided between the ways of the bow and arrow. annotation.summary: Since the common people were powerless, they intended to carry the mikoshi from the Northern Gate and the Nōdono camp. On that day, Shō wore a properly made hitatare, a suit of armor dyed with small cherry blossoms in yellow, carried a copper-colored tachi, bore white-feathered arrows, and had a Shitō bow tucked at his side; he took off his helmet and hung it on a high cord. text: といふ名歌仕て、御感に預る程のやさしき男に、時に臨んで、いかがなさけなう耻辱をば與ふべき。此神輿かき返し奉れや。」と僉議しければ、數千人の大衆、先陣より後陣まで、皆尤々とぞ同じける。さて神輿を先立てまゐらせて、東の陣頭待賢門より入れ奉らむとしければ、狼藉忽に出來て、武士ども散々に射奉る。十禪師の御輿にも、矢どもあまた射立たり。神人宮仕射殺され、衆徒多く疵を被る。をめき叫ぶ聲梵天までも聞え、堅牢地神も驚くらんとぞ覺えける。大衆神輿をば、陣頭に振り棄て奉り、泣く／＼本山へ歸り上る。

annotation.translation: They deliberated, saying, 'Since he is a man of such gentle spirit that he has received such praise for his famous song, how should we show him pity and shame in accordance with the occasion? Let us overturn this palanquin.' Thus, thousands of the common people, from the vanguard to the rearguard, all agreed unanimously. Then, leading the palanquin ahead, they intended to enter through the Tōmon Gate of the eastern camp, but suddenly a riot broke out, and the warriors shot at them indiscriminately. Many arrows struck the palanquin of the Tenshi. The shrine priests, serving the palace, were killed, and many lay followers were wounded. The wailing and shouting could be heard even up to the heavens, and one felt that even the Kōrō-jinjin must have been startled. The multitude cast the palanquin aside at the camp headquarters and, sobbing, returned to the main temple.

text: 藏人の左少辨兼光に仰せて、殿上にて、俄に公卿僉議あり。保安四年七月に、神輿入洛の時は座主に仰せて、赤山の社へ入れ奉る。又保延四年四月に、神輿入洛の時は、祇園の別當に仰せて、祇園の社へ入れ奉る。今度は保延の例たるべしとて、祇園の別當權大僧都澄兼に仰て、秉燭に及で、祇園の社へ入奉る。神輿に立つ所の箭をば、神人してこれを拔かせらる。山門の大衆、日吉の神輿を陣頭へ振奉ること、永久より以降、治承までは六箇度なり。毎度に武士を召てこそ防がれけれども神輿射奉ること、是始とぞ奉る。「靈神怒をなせば、災害岐に滿つといへり。怖し怖し。」とぞ人々申合はれける。

annotation.translation: He ordered the Dainagon, Sashonoi, Kenmitsu, and, in the palace, suddenly there was a joint deliberation by the court nobles. In the fourth year of Hoan, in the seventh month, when the mikoshi entered Kyoto, he ordered the Zushu to place it in the Akayama shrine. Again, in the fourth year of Hoen, in the fourth month, when the mikoshi entered Kyoto, he ordered the Daitokuji of Gion to place it in the Gion shrine. This time, deeming it should follow the precedent of Hoen, he ordered the Gion's Daitokuji, Gon-Daisojo Sumitsune, and, as the candlelight waned, he had it brought into the Gion shrine. The arrows standing on the mikoshi were made to be removed by the shinjin. The great congregation of Mount Hiei and the lifting of the Hiei mikoshi to the vanguard, from the Eikyū era onward until the Jishō era, occurred six times. In each instance, warriors were summoned to provide protection, yet the shooting of the mikoshi is said to have begun with this. "If the divine spirit becomes angry, disasters will fill the land," so the people said in unison, "How terrible, how terrible."

text: 同十四日夜半ばかり、山門の大衆、又下洛すと聞えしかば、夜中に主上腰輿に召して、院の御所法住寺殿へ行幸なる。中宮は御車に奉て、行啓あり。小松の大臣、直衣に箭負て供奉せらる。嫡子權亮少將維盛、束帶に平胡録負て參られけり。關白殿を始め奉て、太政大臣以下の公卿、殿上人、我も／＼と馳せ參る。凡京中の貴賤、禁中の上下、噪ぎのゝしること夥し。山門には神輿に箭立ち、神人宮仕射殺され、衆徒多く疵を被りしかば、大宮、二宮以下、講堂、中堂、すべて諸堂一宇も殘さず皆燒拂て、山野にまじはるべきよし、三千一同に僉議しけり。是によて大衆の申す所、御はからひあるべしと聞えしかば、山門の上綱等、子細を衆徒に觸れむとて、登山したりけるを、大衆おこて西坂本より皆おかへす。

annotation.translation: Around the midnight of the fourteenth day of that month, when it was reported that the multitude from the mountain gate had again descended to the capital, the Emperor was summoned into a palanquin in the middle of the night, and he went in person to the Imperial Palace of In no Gosho, Hōjū-ji. The Empress was carried in a carriage, and she made a progress. The Minister of the Left, Komatsu, donned his ceremonial robe and carried a bow as an attendant. His legitimate son, the Junior Vice-Minister of the Left, Taira no Tomomori, wore the formal court attire, carried a flat quiver, and came. Starting with the Grand Councilor, the State Ministers and below, the high-ranking courtiers, and the court nobles, each and every one rushed to attend. In all, the high and low in the capital, the upper and lower in the inner palace, made a great commotion and clamor. At the mountain gate, arrows were fixed to the portable shrines, the shrine priests serving the gods were shot dead, and many of the monks and priests were wounded. Therefore, the Great Palace, the Second Palace, the Lecture Hall, the Main Hall, and all other halls were completely burned down, and it was decided unanimously by the three thousand men that they should be scattered among the mountains and fields. When it was reported that the multitude had submitted their demands and that there was some imperial consideration, the head monks of the mountain gate, intending to explain the details to the monks and priests, ascended the mountain, but the multitude rose up and sent them all back from Nishi-Sakamoto.

text: 平大納言時忠卿、その時はいまだ左衞門督にておはしけるが、上卿に立つ。大講堂の庭に三塔會合して、上卿を取てひはらんとす。「しや冠打ち落せ、その身を搦めて、湖に沈めよ。」などぞ僉議しける。既にかうと見えけるに、時忠卿、「暫くしづまられ候へ。衆徒の御中へ申すべきこと有り。」とて、懷より小硯疊紙を取出し、一筆書いて大衆の中へ遣す。是を披いて見れば、「衆徒の濫惡を致すは魔縁の所行なり。明王の制止を加ふるは、善逝の加護なり。」とこそ書かれたれ。是を見て、ひはるに及ばず、皆尤々と同じて、谷々へおり、坊々へぞ入にける。一紙一句をもて、三塔三千の憤をやすめ、公私の耻を逃れ給へる時忠卿こそゆゝしけれ。人々も山門の大衆は、發向のかまびすしきばかりかと思たれば、理も存知したりけりとぞ、感ぜられける。

annotation.translation: The Great Councilor Tokitada, at that time still serving as Left Gate Chief, took the position of the Highest Prelate. Gathering at the courtyard of the Great Lecture Hall, the three towers convened to depose the Highest Prelate. They deliberated, saying, 'Cast off his crown, bind his body, and cast him into the lake.' Although it seemed clear that this would be done, Councilor Tokitada said, 'Please remain silent for a moment. I have something to say to the assembly.' He then took out a small inkstone and folded paper from his sleeve, wrote a single letter, and sent it into the midst of the great crowd. When this was opened and read, it said, 'The misconduct of the monks is the work of evil karmic bonds. The intervention of the Ming Kings is the protection of the Well-Gone Ones.' Upon seeing this, before the matter of deposition could even be carried out, all, agreeing entirely, descended into the valleys and entered the temples. By a single sheet and a single sentence, he soothed the anger of the three towers and three thousand, escaped the shame of both public and private affairs, and it was truly remarkable that Councilor Tokitada should have done so. The people also felt that they had been mistaken in thinking the Great Assembly of Mount Hiei was merely noisy in its intent, realizing that it possessed understanding.

text: 同廿日、花山院權中納言忠親卿を上卿にて、國司加賀守師高つひに闕官せられて、尾張の井戸田へ流されけり。目代近藤判官師經禁獄せらる。又去る十三日神輿射奉し武士六人獄定せらる。左衞門尉藤原正純、右衞門尉正季、左衞門尉大江家兼、右衞門尉同家國、左兵衞尉清原康家、右兵衞尉同康友、是等は皆小松殿の侍なり。

annotation.translation: On the 20th of that month, Prince Tadahisa, the Right Middle Counselor of the Flower Mountain Court, was appointed as the senior counselor; the provincial governor Kaga no Kami Mochitaka was ultimately stripped of his office and exiled to Idota in Owari. The temporary governor Kondo no Gonji Toshiyasu was imprisoned. Furthermore, on the 13th of the previous month, six samurai who had shot and presented the portable shrine were sentenced to imprisonment: Saemon no Jō Fujiwara no Masazumi, Uemon no Jō Masanori, Saemon no Jō Ōe no Iekane, Uemon no Jō Tōie, Sabiemon no Jō Kiyohara no Yasuie, and Ubiemon no Jō Tō Yasutomo; all of these were retainers of Lord Komatsu.

text:
同四月二十八日亥刻ばかりに、樋口富小路より火出來て、辰巳の風烈しう吹きければ、京中多く燒にけり。大なる車輪の如くなるほむらが、三町五町を隔てゝ、戌亥の方へすぢかへに、飛び越え／＼燒け行けば、怖しなどもおろかなり。或は具平親王の千種殿、或は北野の天神の紅梅殿、橘逸勢のはひ松殿、鬼殿、高松殿、鴨居殿、東三條、冬嗣の大臣の閑院殿、昭宣公の堀川殿、これを始めて、昔今の名所三十餘箇所、公卿の家だにも、十六箇所まで燒にけり。その外殿上人、諸大夫の家々は注すに及ばず。はては大内に吹きつけて、朱雀門より始めて、應天門、會昌門、大極殿、豐樂院、諸司、八省、朝所、一時がうちに灰燼の地とぞなりにける。家々の日記、代々の文書、
七珍萬寶さながら塵灰となりぬ。その間の費如何ばかりぞ。人の燒け死ぬること數百人、牛馬の類は數を知らず。これ徒事にあらず、山王の御咎とて、比叡山より大なる
猿共が、二三千おりくだり、手に手に松火をともいて、京中を燒くとぞ、人の夢には見えたりける。大極殿は清和天皇の御宇、貞觀十八年に始めて燒けたりければ、同十九年正月三日、陽成院の御即位は、豐樂院にてぞありける。元慶元年四月九日事始ありて同二年十月八日にぞ造り出されたりける。後冷泉院の御宇、天喜五年二月二十六日、又やけにけり。治歴四年八月十四日事始ありしかども、造りいだされずして、後冷泉院崩御なりぬ。後三條院の御宇、延久四年四月十五日造り出して、文人詩を作り奉り、伶人樂を奏して遷幸なし奉る。今は世末になて、國の力も皆衰たれば、その後
はつひに造られず。

annotation.translation: On the 28th day of that same month, around the hour of the Boar, a fire broke out from Higuchi no Tomikoji, and because the wind from the northeast blew fiercely, much of the capital was burned. The flames, like great wheels, leaped across three or five cho, flying straight toward the southwest, and it was so terrifying that fear was cast aside. Beginning with Prince Tadahira's Chikusa no miya, or the Red Plum Hall of the Kannon at Kitano, or the Tachibana no Hayanari's Hibi-no-matsu Hall, Oni Hall, Takamatsu Hall, Kamui Hall, Higashi Sanjo, the Kanmu no Dainagon's Kanna-in Hall, the Shosen no Kyo's Horikawa Hall, and continuing from there, more than thirty famous places of past and present, even up to sixteen noble families' residences, were burned. Besides, the residences of the court nobles and other officials need not be mentioned. Finally, the fire blew into the Inner Palace, and from the Suzaku Gate onward, the Oten Gate, the Kaicho Gate, the Daigoku-den, the Horaku-in, the various offices, the Eight Ministries, the Chosho, in an instant it all became a land of ashes. The family diaries and hereditary documents, the Seven Treasures and Ten Thousand Jewels, all turned to dust and ash. How much did the expenditure amount to? Several hundred people burned to death, and the number of cattle and horses is unknown. This was not mere coincidence; it was said to be the punishment of the Sanno, and from Mt. Hiei, great numbers of monkeys, two or three thousand, descended, holding pine torches in their hands, and it was seen in people's dreams that they were burning the capital. The Daigoku-den was first burned during the reign of Emperor Kammu, in the 18th year of Jogan, so when Emperor Uda ascended the throne on the 3rd day of the 1st month of the 19th year of Jogan, it was held at the Horaku-in. Construction began on the 9th day of the 4th month of the 1st year of Genkyo, and it was completed on the 8th day of the 10th month of the 2nd year of Genkyo. During the reign of Emperor Go-Suzaku, on the 26th day of the 2nd month of the 5th year of Tenki, it burned again. Construction began on the 14th day of the 8th month of the 4th year of Chiryo, but it was not completed, and Emperor Go-Suzaku passed away. During the reign of Emperor Go-Sandajo, it was rebuilt on the 15th day of the 4th month of the 4th year of Enkyu, where a literary poem was presented and musicians performed music, and the emperor was enthroned. Now that the world has come to an end, and the nation's strength has declined in every way, it has never been rebuilt since.

During the reign of Emperor Go-Sandajo, it was rebuilt on the 15th day of the 4th month of the 4th year of Enkyu, where a literary poem was presented and musicians performed music, and the emperor was enthroned. Now that the world has come to an end, and the nation's strength has declined in every way, it has never been rebuilt since.
